---

### Class overrides

#### Slot → element

| Slot | Element |
|------|---------|
| `root` | The avatar's outer element, which carries size and shape. |
| `control` | Inner wrapper around the image, initials or fallback. |
| `image` | The `<img>` element. |
| `fallback` | The initials text element. |
| `status` | The status indicator dot. |
| `loading` | The skeleton's bag — `AvatarShimmer` is a component, and this is what it paints. |

`AvatarGroup` has its own map: `root` (the overlapping row), `item` (each
avatar's wrapper, where the stack margin lives) and `surplus` (the `+N` disc).
`AvatarShimmer` has `root`.

**`surplus` sets the fill and the text, not the ring.** The ring around the
surplus disc is an inline `box-shadow`, cut against the page ground so the disc
sits in the stack the way the avatars beside it do. An inline style beats any
class, so `classes={{ surplus: "ring-2 ring-cl-accent" }}` will not change it —
use `surplus` for background, colour, weight and radius, and take the ring as
given. This is a v1 limitation, stated rather than worked around.

#### CSS custom properties

Set on the avatar's own element by the auto-colour logic, and read by its
classes. You do not normally write them — they are listed because a consumer
overriding `classes.root` with a plain background will find these underneath.

| Variable | Controls | Default |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--avatar-bg` | The generated background in the light theme. | derived from the name's hash |
| `--avatar-text` | The initials colour in the light theme. | derived with the background |
| `--avatar-border` | The ring colour in the light theme. | derived with the background |
| `--avatar-dark-bg` | The generated background in the dark theme. | derived from the name's hash |
| `--avatar-dark-text` | The initials colour in the dark theme. | derived with the background |
| `--avatar-dark-border` | The ring colour in the dark theme. | derived with the background |
| `--cl-bg` | Read, not set: the page ground the group's rings are cut against. | the theme's background token |

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** (`unstyled=false`, no `classes`): Uses `DEFAULT_AVATAR_CLASSES` — minimal layout styles.
2. **Partial override** (`unstyled=false`, partial `classes`) — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** (`unstyled=true`): All slots are empty. You provide everything.

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
┌─ root (outer container, sets size/shape) ──────────────┐
│                                                         │
│  ┌─ control (absolute inset, overflow hidden) ─────────┐ │
│  │                                                    │ │
│  │  <img class="image" />                            │ │
│  │  — OR —                                           │ │
│  │  <span class="fallback">JD</span>                │ │
│  │  — OR —                                           │ │
│  │  <span class="fallback">{icon}</span>            │ │
│  │                                                    │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                         │
│  <span class="status" /> (positioned absolute)          │
│                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot / Prop | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------|-------|
| Overall size | `size` prop | Preset or number. Don't use CSS for this. |
| Shape (circle/square) | `shape` prop | Controls border-radius inline. |
| Background color (initials) | `autoColor` + `colors` | Hash-based. Or use `classes.root` with bg class. |
| Initials font style | `textStyle` prop or `classes.initials` | `textStyle` for inline, `classes.initials` for Tailwind. |
| Image fit/filter | `classes.image` or `imageConfig.className` | Add `object-cover`, `grayscale`, etc. |
| Border ring | `bordered` prop | `true`, or CSS string like `"3px solid gold"`. |
| Status dot color | `status` as config: `{ type: "online", color: "#00ff00" }` | Or override `classes.status`. |
| Ring between grouped avatars | AvatarGroup `ringColor` | Match to your page background. |
| Overlap spacing | AvatarGroup `spacing` | Negative = overlap, positive = gap. |

#### Dark mode

Avatar relies on inline styles for most visual properties (size, shape, auto-generated colors). The `classes` defaults have minimal color classes. When overriding slots, provide `dark:` variants:

```tsx
<Avatar
  name="Jane"
  classes={{
    root: "ring-2 ring-gray-200 dark:ring-gray-700",
    fallback: "text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200",
  }}
/>
```

For grouped avatars, match `ringColor` to your background:

```tsx
<AvatarGroup ringColor={isDarkMode ? "#111827" : "white"}>
  ...
</AvatarGroup>
```

#### Styling via autoColor

`autoColor` generates deterministic colors from the `name` hash. Override the palette with `colors`:

```tsx
<Avatar
  name="Alice"
  autoColor
  colors={{
    backgrounds: ["#ede9fe", "#dbeafe", "#d1fae5", "#fef9c3"],
    text: ["#7c3aed", "#1d4ed8", "#047857", "#854d0e"],
  }}
/>
```

#### Complete themed example: "Slack-style" user list

```tsx
<AvatarGroup
  maxVisible={4}
  spacing={-6}
  ringColor="#1a1d21"
  showTooltip
  layout="stack"
>
  <Avatar
    src="/avatars/alice.jpg"
    name="Alice Chen"
    size="sm"
    shape="rounded"
    status="online"
  />
  <Avatar name="Bob Park" size="sm" shape="rounded" autoColor status="away" />
  <Avatar name="Charlie Kim" size="sm" shape="rounded" autoColor status="offline" />
  <Avatar name="Diana Lee" size="sm" shape="rounded" autoColor status="busy" />
  <Avatar name="Edward Wu" size="sm" shape="rounded" autoColor />
  <Avatar name="Fiona Xu" size="sm" shape="rounded" autoColor />
</AvatarGroup>
```

---

### Patterns

#### Image with fallback to initials

```tsx
<Avatar
  src={user.avatarUrl}
  name={user.displayName}
  onError={() => console.log("Image failed, showing fallback")}
/>
```

#### Badge notification on avatar

```tsx
<div className="relative inline-block">
  <Avatar name="John" src="/john.jpg" />
  <AvatarBadge count={5} position="top-right" variant="solid" pulse />
</div>
```

#### Loading → loaded transition

```tsx
{isLoading ? (
  <AvatarGroupShimmer count={4} showCount />
) : (
  <AvatarGroup maxVisible={4}>
    {users.map(u => (
      <Avatar key={u.id} name={u.name} src={u.avatar} autoColor />
    ))}
  </AvatarGroup>
)}
```

#### Standalone surplus count

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
  <AvatarGroup maxVisible={3}>
    {users.slice(0, 3).map(u => <Avatar key={u.id} name={u.name} autoColor />)}
  </AvatarGroup>
  <AvatarGroupCount count={users.length - 3} variant="ghost" />
</div>
```

#### Clickable avatars in group

```tsx
<AvatarGroup
  maxVisible={5}
  onAvatarClick={(info, event) => {
    console.log(`Clicked ${info.name} at index ${info.index}`);
    navigate(`/users/${info.name}`);
  }}
>
  {users.map(u => <Avatar key={u.id} name={u.name} autoColor />)}
</AvatarGroup>
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

Only an avatar with `onClick` is focusable; a plain one is an image and takes no keyboard input.

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves focus to a clickable avatar, and to the overflow count in an `AvatarGroup`. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Activates it, firing the same `onClick` a pointer would. |

---

### Anti-patterns

```tsx
// ❌ DON'T: Use autoColor without name — it needs name to hash
<Avatar autoColor />
// ✅ DO: Provide name for autoColor
<Avatar name="John" autoColor />

// ❌ DON'T: Expect fallback to show when name is also provided
// Initials from name take priority over fallback
<Avatar name="John" fallback={<UserIcon />} />
// ✅ DO: Use fallback only when no name is available
<Avatar fallback={<UserIcon />} />

// ❌ DON'T: Set explicit size on children when group provides it
<AvatarGroup size="lg">
  <Avatar name="A" size="sm" /> {/* overrides group context */}
</AvatarGroup>
// ✅ DO: Let children inherit from group
<AvatarGroup size="lg">
  <Avatar name="A" />
</AvatarGroup>

// ❌ DON'T: Use white ringColor on dark backgrounds
<div className="bg-gray-900">
  <AvatarGroup>{/* white rings visible */}</AvatarGroup>
</div>
// ✅ DO: Match ringColor to background
<AvatarGroup ringColor="#111827">{/* clean overlap */}</AvatarGroup>
```

---

---

## Breadcrumb

> A navigation trail showing the user's current location in a hierarchy. Supports truncation with a dropdown for collapsed items, custom separators, icons, links, tooltips, and full style customization.

**Category:** Navigation
**Keywords:** breadcrumb, navigation, trail, path, hierarchy, crumb, truncation

### Import

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from "@chumlab/ui/breadcrumb";
import type { BreadcrumbItem } from "@chumlab/ui/breadcrumb";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from "@chumlab/ui/breadcrumb";

export default function PageHeader() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb
      items={[
        { id: "home", label: "Home" },
        { id: "products", label: "Products" },
        { id: "electronics", label: "Electronics" },
        { id: "phones", label: "Phones" },
      ]}
      onItemClick={(item) => console.log("Navigate to:", item.label)}
    />
  );
}
```

This renders correctly with no additional props, classes, or setup. The last item ("Phones") is automatically styled as the active page.

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `items` | **Required.** Must have at least one item. Last item is always treated as the active/current page. |
| `maxVisible` | When total items exceed this, middle items collapse into an ellipsis dropdown. First item and last N-1 items remain visible. |
| `separator` | One prop for text or an icon between items, rendered as given. `iconSize` sizes only the default chevron. |
| `href` on items | Renders the item as `<a>` instead of `<button>`. Disabled items always render as `<button>` regardless of `href`. |
| `item.onClick` | Per-item click overrides the global `onItemClick`. Both can coexist — per-item runs first. |
| `showTooltips` | Enables tooltips globally. Individual items still need `tooltip` content set. |
| `dropdownSide` | Only affects the collapsed items dropdown, not individual items. Options: top, bottom, left, right. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

- `data-truncated="true"` — on root `<nav>` when items are truncated
- `data-dropdown-open="true"` — on root `<nav>` when ellipsis dropdown is open
- `data-state="active|inactive"` — on each item (last item is "active")
- `data-position` — on the collapsed-items menu, the side it resolved to
- `data-breadcrumb-dropdown-id` — on that menu, tying it to the trigger that owns it
- `data-side="top" | "bottom"` — on that menu's surface, the side it was placed on after any flip
- `data-disabled="true"` — on disabled items
- `data-clickable="true"` — on interactive (non-active, non-disabled) items
- `aria-current="page"` — on the last (active) item

**DOM nesting:** `<nav>` → `<ol>` → `<li>` items interleaved with `<li role="presentation">` separators

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from Breadcrumb.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `items` **(required)** | array | — | List of breadcrumb items to render. |
| `maxVisible` | number | `4` | Maximum visible items before collapsing into an ellipsis dropdown. |
| `separator` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the default chevron between items: text or an icon, rendered as given. `iconSize` sizes the default one. |
| `onItemClick` | object | — | (item: BreadcrumbItem) => void — Called when a breadcrumb item is clicked. |
| `aria-label` | string | — | Accessible label for the breadcrumb nav element. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for breadcrumb sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling. |
| `className` | string | — | CSS class for the root element. |
| `style` | object | — | CSSProperties — Inline styles for the root element. |
| `ellipsisIcon` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the collapsed-items button's glyph. Rendered as given; `iconSize` sizes the default one. |
| `iconSize` | number \| string | `16` | Size of breadcrumb icons. |
| `showTooltips` | boolean | `true` | Enables tooltips on breadcrumb items. |
| `tooltipSide` | `"top"` \| `"right"` \| `"bottom"` \| `"left"` | `"bottom"` | Default tooltip position for all items. |
| `tooltipOffset` | number | `4` | Default tooltip offset in pixels. |
| `defaultTooltipProps` | object | — | Default tooltip configuration for all items. |
| `ellipsisTooltip` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Tooltip content for the ellipsis button. |
| `ellipsisTooltipProps` | object | — | Tooltip configuration for the ellipsis button. |
| `dropdownSide` | `"top"` \| `"bottom"` \| `"left"` \| `"right"` | `"top"` | Position of the overflow dropdown. |
| `dropdownZIndex` | number | `50` | Z-index of the overflow dropdown. |
| `portalContainer` | object | — | HTMLElement \| null — Portal container for the dropdown. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Keeps the collapsed-items menu mounted while closed. |
| `ellipsisAriaLabel` | string | `"Show collapsed breadcrumb items"` | Accessible label for the ellipsis button. |
| `onDropdownOpenChange` | object | — | (open: boolean) => void — Called when the dropdown open state changes. |

### Ref API

Forwards ref to the root `<nav>` element:

```tsx
const navRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
<Breadcrumb ref={navRef} items={items} />
// navRef.current is the <nav> DOM element
```

---

### Class overrides

#### Slot → element

| Slot | Element |
|------|---------|
| `root` | The `<nav>` container. |
| `list` | The `<ol>`. |
| `item` | A non-active item. |
| `link` | An item rendered as an anchor, when it has `href`. |
| `itemIcon` | An item's icon. |
| `separator` | The separator between items. |
| `ellipsis` | The `<li>` standing in for collapsed items. |
| `ellipsisTrigger` | The button inside it. |
| `content` | The menu those collapsed items open into. |
| `collapsedItem` | One item inside that menu. |

There is no `linkAndItem` slot. The anchor's combined class is composed
internally from `item` and `link`; override those two.

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** (`unstyled=false`, no `classes`): Uses `DEFAULT_BREADCRUMB_CLASSES` with dark mode support.
2. **Partial override** (`unstyled=false`, partial `classes`) — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** (`unstyled=true`): All slots empty. You provide everything.

```tsx
// `item` carries the base AND 2 state variants. Overriding it
// replaces all of them, so write them together:
<Breadcrumb
  classes={{
    item:
      "rounded-cl-md px-2 py-1 " +           // base
      "data-[disabled]:opacity-50 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed " +
      "data-[state=active]:text-cl-accent ",
  }}
/>

// Passing only `item: "data-[disabled]:…"` drops the base and the other
// 1 states.
```

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
┌─ root ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                              │
│  ┌─ list (<ol>) ──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │                                                         │ │
│  │  [item/link] [separator] [ellipsisTrigger] [separator]  │ │
│  │  [item/link] [separator] [item data-state=active]      │ │
│  │                                                         │ │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                              │
│  ┌─ content (portal) ──────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  [collapsedItem] [collapsedItem] ...                    │   │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------|-------|
| Trail container layout | `list` | Flex container for items + separators. |
| Inactive item styling | `item` | Buttons/spans for non-link, non-active items. |
| Active (last) item styling | `item` + `data-[state=active]:` | The current page is the same slot in a state. |
| Disabled item look |  | Appended to `item` class when disabled. |
| Link items (with href) | `link` | Anchors — separate slot from `item`. |
| Separator icon/text | `separator` | Between each item. |
| Icon inside items | `itemIcon` | Applied to the icon wrapper span. |
| Ellipsis "..." button | `ellipsisTrigger` | The collapse trigger. |
| Collapsed items dropdown | `content` | The portal-rendered menu container. |
| Items inside dropdown | `collapsedItem` | Each collapsed item in the menu. |

#### Dark mode

Default classes use Tailwind `dark:` prefix. Activated by `<html class="dark">`.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={items}
  classes={{
    item: "text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400 hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 data-[state=active]:text-gray-900 data-[state=active]:font-semibold dark:data-[state=active]:text-white",
    content: "bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700",
  }}
/>
```

#### Styling via data attributes

```tsx
// Highlight active item with data-state
<Breadcrumb classes={{
  item: "[&[data-state=active]]:font-bold [&[data-state=active]]:text-blue-600",
}} />
```

```css
/* Truncation-aware styling */
nav[data-truncated="true"] { border: 1px dashed orange; }
nav[data-dropdown-open="true"] .ellipsis-btn { background: blue; }
```

#### Complete themed example: "Pill-style" breadcrumb

```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={items}
  onItemClick={handleClick}
  unstyled
  classes={{
    list: "flex items-center gap-1",
    item: "px-3 py-1.5 text-xs font-medium rounded-full cursor-pointer transition-all bg-gray-100 dark:bg-gray-800 text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400 hover:bg-gray-200 dark:hover:bg-gray-700 data-[state=active]:bg-blue-600 data-[state=active]:text-white",
    separator: "text-gray-300 dark:text-gray-600 mx-0.5",
    ellipsisTrigger: "px-2 py-1 rounded-full bg-gray-100 dark:bg-gray-800 text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400 hover:bg-gray-200 dark:hover:bg-gray-700 cursor-pointer",
    content: "rounded-xl shadow-lg py-1 bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700",
    collapsedItem: "px-3 py-2 text-sm cursor-pointer text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-700",
  }}
/>
```

---

### Patterns

#### Truncated trail with dropdown callback

```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={deepPath}
  maxVisible={3}
  onDropdownOpenChange={(open) => console.log("Dropdown:", open ? "opened" : "closed")}
  onItemClick={(item) => router.push(item.href ?? "/")}
/>
```

#### Items with icons

```tsx
const items: BreadcrumbItem[] = [
  { id: "home", label: "Home", itemIcon: <HomeIcon className="w-4 h-4" /> },
  { id: "docs", label: "Docs", itemIcon: <FolderIcon className="w-4 h-4" /> },
  { id: "api", label: "API Reference" },
];

<Breadcrumb items={items} />
```

#### Link-based navigation

```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={[
    { id: "home", label: "Home", href: "/" },
    { id: "blog", label: "Blog", href: "/blog" },
    { id: "post", label: "Current Post" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Custom separator

```tsx
// String separator
<Breadcrumb items={items} separator={<span className="mx-1 text-gray-400">/</span>} />

// An icon goes through the same prop, rendered as given (iconSize sizes only the default chevron)
<Breadcrumb items={items} separator={<ArrowRightIcon size={14} />} />
```

#### Loading state

```tsx
{isLoading ? (
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <div className="h-4 w-16 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded animate-pulse" />
    <div className="h-4 w-20 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded animate-pulse" />
    <div className="h-4 w-24 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded animate-pulse" />
  </div>
) : (
  <Breadcrumb items={items} onItemClick={handleClick} />
)}
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves through the crumbs, and to the ellipsis trigger when the trail is collapsed. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Follows a crumb, or opens the collapsed-items menu from the ellipsis. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | Moves between items inside the open menu. |
| `Home`, `End` | Jumps to the first or last item in the menu. |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the ellipsis. Always: there is no prop to turn it off, because the APG menu button pattern requires Escape to close the menu. |

---

---

## Button

> A polymorphic, accessible button that renders as `<button>`, `<a>`, or `<span>`. Provides structural defaults (padding, focus ring, disabled state) — visual theme is applied via `className`. Supports icons with animations, loading states, tooltips, and grouping.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** button, action, submit, link, cta, icon, loading, group

### Import

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from "@chumlab/ui/button";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from "@chumlab/ui/button";

export default function Actions() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup>
      <Button
        className="bg-indigo-600 dark:bg-indigo-500 text-white hover:bg-indigo-500 dark:hover:bg-indigo-400 shadow-md"
        onClick={() => console.log("clicked")}
      >
        Save Changes
      </Button>
      <Button
        className="border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-800"
      >
        Cancel
      </Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

**Why className, not a `variant` prop?** Button is intentionally headless for visual styling. The component owns interaction (focus, disabled, loading, polymorphic rendering) while you own the look. This avoids a closed set of variants and gives full design freedom.

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `as="a"` | Requires `href`. Without it, TypeScript errors. |
| `as="span"` | Needs `aria-label` if no text content — dev warning in console. |
| `asChild` | Mutually exclusive with `as`. Child must be a single valid React element. |
| `loading` | Makes the button disabled automatically. No need to also set `disabled`. |
| `iconAnimation` | Only animates when `as` is not "span" (needs `group` class which is auto-added). |
| `animateOnHover` | `true` = animate on hover only. `false` = continuous animation (always running). |
| `animateIcon` | Controls which icon(s) animate: `"leading"`, `"trailing"`, or `"both"`. |
| `className` vs `classes.root` | Both are applied via `cn()`. `className` comes last (highest CSS priority). `classes.root` composes with the root's defaults. Don't use both for the same concern. |

---

### How `className` merges with defaults

This is the most important thing to understand:

```typescript
// Inside Button.tsx:
const combinedClassName = cn(
  mergedClasses.root,    // DEFAULT_BUTTON_CLASSES.root (structural)
  fullWidth && "w-full",
  animation && "group",
  className,             // YOUR className (visual theme) — applied LAST
);
```

The default `root` provides: `cursor-pointer text-sm font-medium px-4 py-2.5 rounded-xl transition-all duration-150 focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:pointer-events-none`

Your `className` adds: colors, backgrounds, shadows, borders — the visual theme.

To override structural defaults (e.g., different padding), include the override in your `className`. Tailwind's last-class-wins behavior handles it.

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

- `data-loading="true"` — when loading
- `data-disabled="true"` — when disabled or loading
- `data-full-width="true"` — when fullWidth
- `data-orientation="horizontal" | "vertical"` — on `ButtonGroup`, from its `orientation` prop
- `data-size="sm|md|lg"` — size prop value
- `data-reduce-motion="true"` — on the loading spinner, while reduced motion is in force
- `aria-busy="true"` — when loading
- `aria-disabled="true"` — when disabled or loading

**DOM:** `<button>` (or `<a>`/`<span>`) → `<span class="content">` → optional `<span class="startIcon">` + children + optional `<span class="endIcon">`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from Button.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Button content. |
| `as` | `"button"` \| `"a"` \| `"span"` | `"button"` | HTML element to render as. |
| `asChild` | boolean | `false` | Merges button props onto a child element via Slot. |
| `size` | `"sm"` \| `"md"` \| `"lg"` | — | Sets padding, type size, gap, icon box and loader together: 28, 40 and 52px tall. Also emits data-size on the root, so CSS can target it; the attribute is a hook, not the mechanism. |
| `disabled` | boolean | — | Disables interaction and applies disabled styling. |
| `startIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Icon rendered before the button label. |
| `endIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Icon rendered after the button label. |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Shows a loading spinner and disables interaction. |
| `loadingContent` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Text displayed alongside the loading spinner. |
| `loaderPosition` | `"start"` \| `"end"` | `"end"` | Which end of the label the loader appears at: `start` before it, `end` after it. |
| `loaderSize` | number | `16` | Pixel size of the loading spinner. |
| `loader` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom loader element replacing the default spinner. |
| `fullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Stretches the button to fill its container width. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for button sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling, rendering a plain element. |
| `iconAnimation` | `"none"` \| `"slideRight"` \| `"slideLeft"` \| `"slideUp"` \| `"slideDown"` \| `"bounce"` \| `"pulse"` \| `"spin"` | `"none"` | Animation applied to icons on hover. |
| `animateOnHover` | boolean | `true` | Enables icon animation on hover. |
| `animateIcon` | `"leading"` \| `"trailing"` \| `"both"` | `"trailing"` | Which icon(s) to animate. |
| `reduceMotion` | boolean \| `"auto"` | `"auto"` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects OS setting. |
| `tooltip` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Tooltip content shown on hover. |
| `tooltipProps` | object | — | Configuration for tooltip positioning and appearance. |
| `href` | string | — | Link destination (required when as='a'). |
| `target` | string | — | Link target attribute (when as='a'). |
| `rel` | string | — | Link rel attribute (when as='a'). |

### Ref API

Forwards ref to the underlying DOM element (type depends on `as`):

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
<Button ref={ref}>Click</Button>
// ref.current is HTMLButtonElement, HTMLAnchorElement, or HTMLSpanElement
```

---

### Sub-component Props

Generated from the types by `scripts/build-subcomponent-schemas.mjs`.

#### ButtonGroup

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Button elements to group together. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal" \| undefined` | Stack direction. Default: `"horizontal"`. |

---

### Class overrides

#### Slot → element

| Slot | Element |
|------|---------|
| `root` | The `<button>`, `<a>` or `<span>` the button renders as. |
| `itemText` | The inner content wrapper around the label. |
| `icon` | The leading or trailing icon wrapper. |
| `loading` | The spinner wrapper shown while `loading`. |

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
┌─ root (button/a/span — structural styles + your className) ─┐
│                                                               │
│  ┌─ itemText (inline-flex wrapper) ─────────────────────────┐ │
│  │                                                          │ │
│  │  [loading?]  [icon]  children  [icon]  [loading?] │ │
│  │                                                          │ │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| "I want to change..." | How | Notes |
|------------------------|-----|-------|
| Button colors/background | `className` | Your primary styling mechanism. |
| Padding/border-radius | `className` (overrides default) | Default is `px-4 py-2.5 rounded-xl`. |
| Focus ring color | `className` | Add `focus-visible:ring-indigo-500` etc. |
| Icon spacing | `classes={{ content: "gap-4" }}` | Default gap is `gap-2`. |
| Icon size/color | Style the icon element itself | Icons are your ReactNode — you control them. |
| Loader appearance | `loading` prop, a `loader` element, or `classes={{ loader: "..." }}` | A `loader` element replaces the default spinner; `classes.loader` adds classes to it. |
| Disabled opacity | `className` | Default is `disabled:opacity-50`. Override with `disabled:opacity-30` etc. |

#### Dark mode

Button defaults have no color classes — they're structural only. Dark mode is handled entirely in your `className`:

```tsx
<Button className="bg-indigo-600 dark:bg-indigo-500 text-white hover:bg-indigo-500 dark:hover:bg-indigo-400 focus-visible:ring-indigo-500 dark:focus-visible:ring-indigo-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900">
  Save
</Button>
```

Always include `dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900` (or your dark bg color) so the focus ring offset doesn't show a white gap.

#### Common variant recipes

Copy-paste these as `className` values:

```tsx
// Primary (indigo)
"bg-indigo-600 dark:bg-indigo-500 text-white hover:bg-indigo-500 dark:hover:bg-indigo-400 active:bg-indigo-700 dark:active:bg-indigo-600 shadow-md shadow-indigo-600/25 dark:shadow-indigo-500/20 focus-visible:ring-indigo-500 dark:focus-visible:ring-indigo-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"

// Secondary (subtle)
"bg-gray-50 dark:bg-white/8 text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-white/[0.14] ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-200 dark:ring-white/[0.1] shadow-sm dark:shadow-none focus-visible:ring-gray-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"

// Outline
"border border-gray-200 dark:border-white/15 text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-white/6 focus-visible:ring-gray-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"

// Ghost (no background)
"text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-white/8 focus-visible:ring-gray-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"

// Danger
"bg-red-500 text-white hover:bg-red-400 active:bg-red-600 shadow-md shadow-red-500/20 focus-visible:ring-red-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"

// Success
"bg-emerald-500 text-white hover:bg-emerald-400 active:bg-emerald-600 shadow-md shadow-emerald-500/20 focus-visible:ring-emerald-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"
```

#### Complete themed example: "Stripe Dashboard" actions

```tsx
<div className="flex gap-2">
  <Button
    className="bg-indigo-600 dark:bg-indigo-500 text-white text-xs px-3 py-1.5 rounded-lg hover:bg-indigo-700 dark:hover:bg-indigo-400 shadow-sm focus-visible:ring-indigo-500 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"
    startIcon={<PlusIcon className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />}
  >
    Create payment
  </Button>
  <Button
    className="text-xs px-3 py-1.5 rounded-lg border border-gray-300 dark:border-gray-600 text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 focus-visible:ring-gray-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"
    startIcon={<FilterIcon className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />}
  >
    Filter
  </Button>
  <Button
    className="text-xs px-3 py-1.5 rounded-lg text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400 hover:text-gray-700 dark:hover:text-gray-200 hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 focus-visible:ring-gray-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-gray-900"
  >
    Export
  </Button>
</div>
```

---

### Patterns

#### Link button

```tsx
<Button as="a" href="/settings" className={primaryClasses}>
  Go to Settings
</Button>
```

#### Loading with feedback

```tsx
const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);

<Button
  className={primaryClasses}
  loading={saving}
  loadingContent="Saving..."
  onClick={async () => {
    setSaving(true);
    await saveData();
    setSaving(false);
  }}
>
  Save
</Button>
```

#### Icon-only with tooltip

```tsx
<Button
  className={iconOnlyClasses}
  startIcon={<TrashIcon />}
  aria-label="Delete item"
  tooltip="Delete"
  tooltipProps={{ side: "bottom", delayDuration: 300 }}
/>
```

#### Button group (segmented control)

```tsx
<ButtonGroup className="inline-flex gap-0">
  <Button className={`${outlineClasses} rounded-r-none border-r-0`}>Left</Button>
  <Button className={`${outlineClasses} rounded-none border-r-0`}>Center</Button>
  <Button className={`${outlineClasses} rounded-l-none`}>Right</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

#### Icon animation on hover

```tsx
<Button
  className={primaryClasses}
  startIcon={<ArrowRightIcon />}
  iconAnimation="slideRight"
>
  Continue
</Button>
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the button. `disabled` and `loading` both remove it from the tab order. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Activates it. With `as="span"` the handler is added for you, since a span has no native activation. |

---

### Anti-patterns

```tsx
// ❌ DON'T: Use as="a" without href
<Button as="a" className="...">Link</Button>
// ✅ DO: Always provide href with as="a"
<Button as="a" href="/page" className="...">Link</Button>

// ❌ DON'T: Nest interactive elements inside Button
<Button><a href="/page">Link inside button</a></Button>
// ✅ DO: Use as="a" for link-style buttons
<Button as="a" href="/page">Link</Button>

// ❌ DON'T: Use color alone for destructive actions
<Button className="bg-red-500 text-white">Delete</Button>
// ✅ DO: Include a warning icon or confirmation
<Button className="bg-red-500 text-white" startIcon={<TrashIcon />}>Delete</Button>

// ❌ DON'T: Use icon-only span button without aria-label
<Button as="span" startIcon={<CloseIcon />} />
// ✅ DO: Always provide aria-label for icon-only buttons
<Button as="span" startIcon={<CloseIcon />} aria-label="Close" />
```

---

### AI Instructions

- **Always provide `className`** — Button has no built-in colors. Without it, you get a transparent, unstyled button.
- **Use `as="a"` for navigation**, `as="button"` for actions. Never use `as="span"` unless the element must be non-focusable-by-default.
- **Always add `aria-label`** to icon-only buttons.
- **`size` sets dimensions now** — sm/md/lg are 28/40/52px tall, with padding, type, gap, icon box and loader moving together. It did not until v1: the prop emitted `data-size` and painted nothing, and this line used to say so. A `className` still wins over any of it — the size tokens are plain utilities in the same merge groups, so `px-8` replaces the size's padding rather than sitting beside it.
- **Safe defaults:** `<Button className="bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700 ...">Label</Button>`.
- **Use `loading` + `loadingContent`** for async actions. The button auto-disables during loading.
- **`disabled` vs `loading`:** both disable interaction, but `loading` shows a spinner and sets `aria-busy`.

---

---

## CascadingDropdown

> A multi-level dropdown menu with nested submenus. Supports single and multi-select per level, async data loading, and search with debounce.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** cascading dropdown, nested menu, multi-level select, submenu, hierarchical, category picker, tree select, async dropdown

### Import

```tsx
import { CascadingDropdown } from "@chumlab/ui/cascading-dropdown";
import type { CascadingOption, CascadingValue } from "@chumlab/ui/cascading-dropdown";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { CascadingDropdown } from "@chumlab/ui/cascading-dropdown";
import type { CascadingOption, CascadingValue } from "@chumlab/ui/cascading-dropdown";
import { useState } from "react";

const options: CascadingOption[] = [
  {
    value: "electronics",
    label: "Electronics",
    children: [
      { value: "phones", label: "Phones" },
      { value: "laptops", label: "Laptops" },
    ],
  },
  {
    value: "clothing",
    label: "Clothing",
    children: [
      { value: "shirts", label: "Shirts" },
      { value: "pants", label: "Pants" },
    ],
  },
];

export default function Example() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<CascadingValue>({});
  return (
    <CascadingDropdown
      options={options}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      placeholder="Select category..."
    />
  );
}
```

This renders correctly with built-in styles, dark mode, and keyboard navigation.

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `selectionMode` on an option | Set on each `CascadingOption.children` parent. `"single"` = radio behavior, `"multi"` = checkbox. Defaults to `"single"`. |
| `loadChildren` | Only called when `option.hasChildren` is true and `option.children` is undefined. Must return `Promise<CascadingOption[]>`. |
| `searchMenu` | When provided, disables client-side menu filtering. You must return filtered results. |
| `searchSubmenu` | When provided, disables client-side submenu filtering. Receives `(query, parent)`. |
| `value` / `onValueChange` | Controlled mode. Shape: `{ parentValue: "childValue" }` for single, `{ parentValue: ["a","b"] }` for multi. |
| `defaultValue` | Uncontrolled mode. Cannot be used with `value`. |
| `closeOnSelect` | Defaults to `true`. Set `false` to keep menu open after selection (useful for multi-select). |
| `classes.subSearchControl` | Falls back to `searchControl` if not set. Same for `subSearchInput` and `subSearchIcon`. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

**Root and trigger:**
- `data-disabled` — when `disabled={true}`
- `data-error` — when `error={true}`
- `data-valid` — when `success={true}` and not `error`
- `data-open` — when dropdown is open
- `data-full-width` — on the root, when `fullWidth`

**Menu items** (top level and submenu):
- `data-highlighted` — the keyboard position
- `data-selected` — a selected option; a selected single-select option shows the selected icon (`showSelectedIcon`)
- `data-disabled` — a disabled option; it takes no focus or highlight, a click or a key does not select it, and a disabled parent does not open its submenu
- `data-has-submenu` — on a top-level item that opens a submenu

**Multi-select checkbox** (inside a `menuitemcheckbox`): `data-state="checked" | "unchecked"`, and `data-checked` while checked

**Surfaces:** `data-cascading-submenu` marks the submenu's surface; `data-side` on each surface is the side it was placed on after any flip

**Messages:** `data-invalid` on the error message, `data-valid` on the success message

- `role="menu"` on the dropdown menu container
- `role="menuitem"` on parent-level menu items
- `role="menuitemcheckbox"` on multi-select submenu items
- `role="menuitemradio"` on single-select submenu items
- `aria-expanded` on trigger and menu items with children
- `aria-checked` on submenu items

DOM nesting: `root > control > trigger + portal(menu > menuItem* + submenu > submenuItem*)`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from CascadingDropdown.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` **(required)** | array | `[]` | Top-level options for the dropdown. |
| `value` | object | — | Controlled selection value as { [parentValue]: string \| string[] }. |
| `defaultValue` | object | — | Initial selection value for uncontrolled usage. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (value: CascadingValue, path: CascadingOption[]) => void |
| `loadChildren` | object | — | (parent: CascadingOption) => Promise<CascadingOption[]> — Async child loader. |
| `onLoadError` | object | — | (error: unknown) => void — Called when async child loading fails. |
| `open` | boolean | — | Controlled open state. |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Initial open state for uncontrolled usage. |
| `onOpenChange` | object | — | (open: boolean) => void |
| `onBlur` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void — Fires when the trigger loses focus, with the native focus event. |
| `onFocus` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void — Fires when the trigger takes focus, with the native focus event. |
| `onKeyDown` | object | — | (event: React.KeyboardEvent) => void |
| `id` | string | — | HTML id attribute. |
| `name` | string | — | Form field name. |
| `placeholder` | object | `"Select an option"` | React.ReactNode — Placeholder content when no value is selected. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables the dropdown. |
| `error` | boolean | `false` | Displays error state. |
| `errorMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Error message. |

| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Description text. |
| `success` | boolean | `false` | Displays success state. |
| `successMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Success message. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Marks the field as required. |
| `emptyContent` | object | `"No options found"` | React.ReactNode — Content shown when no results match. |
| `loadingContent` | object | `"Loading..."` | React.ReactNode — Text shown during async loading. |
| `shimmerCount` | number | — | Number of shimmer placeholders during loading. |
| `loading` | boolean | — | Shows loading state. |
| `clearable` | boolean | `false` | Shows a clear button to reset the selection. |
| `showChevron` | boolean | `true` | Shows a chevron indicator on the trigger. |
| `showSelectedIcon` | boolean | `true` | Shows an icon on selected items. |
| `selectedIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom icon for selected items. |
| `checkboxIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom checkbox icon for multi-select. |
| `fullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Stretches the dropdown to fill its container width. |
| `submenuSide` | `"start"` \| `"end"` | `"end"` | The side submenus open on, logical: `"end"` is the right in a left-to-right page and the left in a right-to-left one, read from the closest `dir` attribute when the submenu opens, else the document's. RTL is not supported in 0.1.0; the values are logical so they need no rename when it is. |
| `dropdownSide` | `"top"` \| `"bottom"` | `"bottom"` | Vertical position of the dropdown. |
| `closeOnSelect` | boolean | `true` | Closes the dropdown after an item is selected. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for dropdown sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling. |
| `lockScroll` | boolean | `false` | Locks body scroll when the dropdown is open. |
| `portalContainer` | object | — | HTMLElement \| null — Portal container for the dropdown. |
| `dropdownZIndex` | number | `50` | Z-index of the dropdown. |
| `dropdownOffset` | number | `4` | Gap in pixels between trigger and dropdown. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Keep the dropdown DOM mounted when closed. |
| `className` | string | — | CSS class for the root element. |
| `style` | object | — | CSSProperties — Inline styles. |
| `clearIcon` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the clear button's glyph. Rendered as given. |
| `renderTrigger` | object | — | (triggerProps: CascadingDropdownTriggerRenderProps, state: CascadingDropdownTriggerState) => ReactNode - Custom render function for the trigger element. Spread triggerProps onto a <button>; draw from state (isOpen, displayValue, placeholder). |
| `showMenuSearch` | boolean | `false` | Show a search input inside the main menu. |
| `showSubmenuSearch` | boolean | `false` | Show a search input inside submenus. |
| `menuSearchPlaceholder` | string | `"Search..."` | Placeholder text for the main menu search input. |
| `submenuSearchPlaceholder` | string | `"Search..."` | Placeholder text for the submenu search input. |
| `searchMenu` | object | — | (query: string) => Promise<CascadingOption[]> — Async search for main menu. |
| `searchSubmenu` | object | — | (query: string, parent: CascadingOption) => Promise<CascadingOption[]> — Async search for submenu. |
| `searchDebounce` | number | `300` | Debounce delay in ms for async search callbacks. |
| `searchIcon` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the search field's magnifier. Rendered as given; `classes.searchIcon` styles the default one. |
| `menuSearchAriaLabel` | string | `"Search menu"` | Accessible label for the menu search input. |
| `submenuSearchAriaLabel` | string | `"Search submenu"` | Accessible label for the submenu search input. |
| `aria-label` | string | — | Accessible label for the dropdown. |
| `aria-labelledby` | string | — | Names the field by another element, and wins over `label` and `aria-label`. Lands on the trigger. |
| `aria-describedby` | string | — | Lands on the trigger, joined with the component's own error message. |

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** (no classes, no unstyled) — uses `DEFAULT_CASCADINGDROPDOWN_CLASSES` with full dark mode
2. **Partial override** (`classes={{ trigger: "..." }}`) — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** (`unstyled={true}`) — all slots empty, you provide everything

```tsx
// `item` carries the base AND 2 state variants. Overriding it
// replaces all of them, so write them together:
<CascadingDropdown
  classes={{
    item:
      "rounded-cl-md px-2 py-1 " +           // base
      "data-[disabled]:opacity-50 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed " +
      "data-[highlighted]:bg-cl-bg-hover ",
  }}
/>

// Passing only `item: "data-[disabled]:…"` drops the base and the other
// 1 states.
```

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root
├── label
├── description
├── control
│   ├── trigger [icon, selectedContent]
│   └── clearTrigger
├── errorMessage / successMessage
└── portal
    ├── content
    │   ├── searchControl [searchIcon + searchInput]
    │   ├── item* [itemIcon]
    │   ├── empty
    │   ├── loading
    │   └── loading > loadingItem*
    └── subPositioner            (its own portal, anchored to the open item)
        └── subContent
            ├── subSearchControl [subSearchIcon + subSearchInput]
            └── subItem* [itemControl data-state=checked, itemIndicator]
```

**`subPositioner` changed meaning in 0.1.0.** It used to be an
`absolute left-full top-0` wrapper *inside* the menu item, so a consumer could
move the submenu by overriding it with their own offsets. It is now the root of
the submenu's own portal, positioned by `useAnchoredPosition` — the same
clamp-and-flip every other floating surface in the package uses. Positioning
utilities on this key no longer do anything: `top`, `left` and `position` are
inline styles, and inline wins. Everything else it carried still applies; the
default value (`z-[9999]`) is unchanged. Use `submenuSide` to choose a side:
`"end"` (the default) or `"start"`, logical, so `"end"` opens right in a
left-to-right page and left in a right-to-left one, read from the closest `dir`
attribute when the submenu opens. RTL is not supported in 0.1.0; the values are
logical so that supporting it later needs no rename. The physical side actually
used, after any flip, is on the element as `data-side`.

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------|-------|
| Trigger button style | `trigger` | |
| Dropdown background | `content` | |
| Menu item hover | `item` | Uses hover: pseudo-class |
| Selected item highlight | `subItem` + `data-selected:` | The selected item is the same slot in a state |
| Focused item (keyboard) | `menuItemFocused` | Stacks on top of menuItem |
| Submenu panel | `subContent` | |
| Checkbox style | `itemControl` + `data-[state=checked]:` | The checked box is the same slot in a state |
| Search bar in menu | `searchControl`, `searchInput`, `searchIcon` | |
| Search bar in submenu | `subSearchControl` | Falls back to `searchControl` if empty |
| Loading state | `loading`, `loading`, `loadingItem` | |

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix, activated by `<html class="dark">`. When overriding a slot, always provide both variants:

```tsx
classes={{
  trigger: "bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 text-black dark:text-white border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700",
}}
```

#### Styling via data attributes

```css
/* Style trigger when open */
[data-open] { border-color: blue; }

/* Style when in message state */
[data-error] { border-color: red; }
```

#### Complete themed example

```tsx
<CascadingDropdown
  unstyled
  options={options}
  value={value}
  onValueChange={setValue}
  placeholder="Pick a category"
  classes={{
    control: "relative w-64",
    trigger: "flex items-center justify-between w-full px-4 py-2.5 rounded-lg border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 text-gray-900 dark:text-white hover:border-blue-400 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500",
    content: "mt-1 rounded-lg shadow-xl bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 py-1",
    item: "px-3 py-2 cursor-pointer text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 hover:bg-blue-50 dark:hover:bg-blue-900/30 flex items-center justify-between",
    subContent: "rounded-lg shadow-xl bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 py-1",
    subItem: "px-3 py-2 cursor-pointer text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 hover:bg-blue-50 dark:hover:bg-blue-900/30 flex items-center gap-2 data-selected:bg-blue-50 data-selected:text-blue-700 dark:data-selected:bg-blue-900/40 dark:data-selected:text-blue-300",
    itemControl: "w-4 h-4 rounded border border-gray-300 dark:border-gray-600 flex items-center justify-center data-[state=checked]:bg-blue-600 data-[state=checked]:border-blue-600 data-[state=checked]:text-white",
    icon: "w-4 h-4 text-gray-400",
  }}
/>
```

---

### Patterns

#### Async data loading (fetch children on hover)

```tsx
const loadChildren = async (parent: CascadingOption) => {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/categories/${parent.value}/children`);
  return res.json();
};

<CascadingDropdown
  options={[
    { value: "electronics", label: "Electronics", hasChildren: true },
    { value: "clothing", label: "Clothing", hasChildren: true },
  ]}
  loadChildren={loadChildren}
  value={value}
  onValueChange={setValue}
/>
```

#### Multi-select with mixed modes

```tsx
const options: CascadingOption[] = [
  {
    value: "colors",
    label: "Colors",
    selectionMode: "multi",
    children: [
      { value: "red", label: "Red" },
      { value: "blue", label: "Blue" },
    ],
  },
  {
    value: "size",
    label: "Size",
    selectionMode: "single",
    children: [
      { value: "sm", label: "Small" },
      { value: "lg", label: "Large" },
    ],
  },
];
```

#### Async search with debounce

```tsx
const searchCountries = async (query: string) => {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/countries/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`);
  const { countries } = await res.json();
  return countries.map((c) => ({ value: c.code, label: c.name }));
};

<CascadingDropdown
  options={regions}
  showMenuSearch
  searchMenu={searchCountries}
  searchDebounce={300}
/>
```

#### Controlled with form integration

```tsx
<CascadingDropdown
  name="category"
  label="Category"
  required
  error={!!errors.category}
  errorMessage={errors.category}
  options={options}
  value={value}
  onValueChange={setValue}
/>
```

---

### Forms

- **Submitted value.** With `name`, it submits one entry, the value object as JSON (`{"fruit":"a"}`), or `{}` when nothing is selected.
- **Reset.** A form reset — a `type="reset"` button or `form.reset()` — restores an uncontrolled selection to `defaultValue` (or `{}`), and the submitted value with it. Like a native input it fires no change callback: `onValueChange` is not called. A controlled CascadingDropdown is left alone: it keeps the `value` you pass and calls nothing, as a controlled React `<input>` does. Reset your own state in the form's `onReset` if you want the field cleared.
- **Required.** A `required` CascadingDropdown needs at least one selection: with none, it blocks the form's submit with the browser's own "fill out this field" message and moves focus to the trigger. The field shows an error state only when you pass `error` and `errorMessage`.
- **Disabled.** A disabled CascadingDropdown submits nothing, as a disabled native control doesn't.

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Enter`, `Space` | Opens the menu from the trigger, and selects the focused item. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | Moves between items in the open menu. |
| `ArrowRight` | Opens the focused item's submenu and moves into it. `ArrowLeft` closes it and returns to the parent. |
| `Home`, `End` | Jumps to the first or last item of the current level. |
| `Escape` | Closes the deepest open menu and returns focus to its trigger. Always: there is no prop to turn it off, because the APG menu button pattern requires Escape to close the menu. |
| `Tab` | Closes the menu and moves focus on. |
| Printable characters | Type-ahead: jumps to the first item starting with what you typed. |

---

### Ref API

The ref lands on the trigger, the menu `<button>` a keyboard user tabs to, so `ref.current.focus()` focuses the field — which is what a form library calls on the first invalid field. With `renderTrigger`, it is the element your trigger attaches `triggerProps.ref` to.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
<CascadingDropdown ref={ref} options={options} />
// ref.current is the trigger <button>
```

---

## Checkbox

> A customizable checkbox with label, description, indeterminate state, custom icons, sizes, shapes, and accessible via native `<input>`.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** checkbox, toggle, check, tick, indeterminate, form input, boolean, selection

### Import

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@chumlab/ui/checkbox";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@chumlab/ui/checkbox";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function Example() {
  const [checked, setChecked] = useState(false);
  return (
    <Checkbox
      label="I agree to the terms"
      checked={checked}
      onCheckedChange={setChecked}
    />
  );
}
```

This renders correctly with no additional props, classes, or setup.

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `defaultChecked` | Uncontrolled mode. Cannot be used with `checked`. |
| `size` | Preset string (`"xs"` to `"xl"`) or number (pixel value). |
| `classes.control` with `data-[state=checked]:` / `data-[state=unchecked]:` | Composes with the control's defaults. A plain utility (`bg-green-500`) wins in every state; a `data-[state=checked]:` one restyles that state only. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

- `data-checked` on root and checkbox span — when checked
- `data-state="checked" | "unchecked" | "indeterminate"` on the box — always
  present, and the one to target; `data-checked` is the presence-only companion
- `data-readonly="true"` on the box — when `readOnly`
- `data-invalid="true"` on the message — when it is the error message
- `data-indeterminate` on root and checkbox span — when indeterminate
- `data-disabled` on checkbox span — when disabled
- `data-error` on checkbox span — when `error={true}`
- `data-size` on root — preset size name (not set for numeric sizes)
- `data-shape` on root — "square", "rounded", or "circle"
- `data-reduce-motion` on root — when reduced motion active
- `data-loading` on root — when loading
- `data-valid` on root — when success state

DOM nesting: `root > label > (checkbox-span > hidden-input + icon) + (labelContainer > label-text + description) + error/success`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from Checkbox.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Text label rendered beside the checkbox. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Helper text rendered below the label. |
| `checked` | boolean | — | Controlled checked state. |
| `defaultChecked` | boolean | `false` | Initial checked state for uncontrolled usage. |
| `indeterminate` | boolean | `false` | Displays the indeterminate (minus) indicator instead of a checkmark. |
| `onCheckedChange` | object | — | (checked: boolean) => void — Fires with the new `checked` state. |
| `onFocus` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent) => void |
| `onBlur` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent) => void |
| `error` | boolean | `false` | Displays the checkbox in an error state. |
| `errorMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Error message displayed below the checkbox. |
| `success` | boolean | `false` | Displays the checkbox in a success state. |
| `successMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Success message displayed below the checkbox. |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Displays the checkbox in a loading state. |
| `size` | `"xs"` \| `"sm"` \| `"md"` \| `"lg"` \| `"xl"` \| number | `"md"` | Size of the checkbox indicator. |
| `shape` | `"square"` \| `"rounded"` \| `"circle"` | `"rounded"` | Shape of the checkbox indicator. |
| `checkedIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom icon for the checked state. |
| `uncheckedIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom icon for the unchecked state. |
| `indeterminateIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom icon for the indeterminate state. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for checkbox sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling. |
| `reduceMotion` | boolean \| `"auto"` | `"auto"` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects OS setting. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables the checkbox. |
| `name` | string | — | Form field name. |
| `value` | string | — | Form field value. |
| `id` | string | — | HTML id attribute. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Marks the checkbox as required. |

### Class overrides

#### Slot → element

| Slot | Element |
|------|---------|
| `root` | The container wrapping the box and its label. Carries every data attribute. |
| `group` | The label and description stacked together. |
| `label` | The label text. |
| `description` | The description under the label. |
| `control` | The indicator box itself. |
| `itemIndicator` | The check or indeterminate glyph inside the box. |
| `message` | The error or success line. |

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** (no classes, no unstyled) — uses `DEFAULT_CHECKBOX_CLASSES` with dark mode
2. **Partial override** (`classes={{ checked: "..." }}`) — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** (`unstyled={true}`) — all slots empty, you provide everything

```tsx
// `control` carries the base AND 3 state variants. Overriding it
// replaces all of them, so write them together:
<Checkbox
  classes={{
    control:
      "rounded-cl-md px-2 py-1 " +           // base
      "data-[state=checked]:bg-cl-accent " +
      "data-[state=indeterminate]:bg-cl-accent/60 " +
      "data-[state=unchecked]:bg-transparent ",
  }}
/>

// Passing only `control: "data-[state=checked]:…"` drops the base and the other
// 2 states.
```

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root
└── label (implicit, wraps everything)
    ├── control [contains hidden input + itemIndicator]
    │   ├── (hidden native input)
    │   └── itemIndicator (check / indeterminate / unchecked)
    └── group
        ├── label (text)
        └── description (text)
message / message (below)
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------|-------|
| Box color when checked | `checked` | Background + border + text color |
| Box color when unchecked | `control` + `data-[state=unchecked]:` | Background + border |
| Box border radius | `control` | Or use `shape` prop |
| Label text style | `label` | Font size, color, weight |
| Error message style | `message` | Color, size |
| Check icon | `itemIndicator` | Or use `checkedIcon` prop for custom element |

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix. When overriding, provide both variants:

```tsx
classes={{
  control:
    "data-[state=checked]:bg-green-600 data-[state=checked]:border-green-600 data-[state=checked]:text-white dark:data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500 dark:data-[state=checked]:border-green-500 data-[state=unchecked]:bg-white data-[state=unchecked]:border-gray-300 dark:data-[state=unchecked]:bg-gray-800 dark:data-[state=unchecked]:border-gray-600",
}}
```

#### Styling via data attributes

```css
[data-checked] .checkbox-label { font-weight: bold; }
[data-error] { border-color: red; }
[data-indeterminate] { opacity: 0.8; }
```

#### Complete themed example

```tsx
<Checkbox
  unstyled
  label="Subscribe to newsletter"
  description="Get weekly updates"
  checked={checked}
  onCheckedChange={setChecked}
  shape="circle"
  classes={{
    root: "",
    control:
      "w-5 h-5 rounded-full border-2 border-gray-300 dark:border-gray-600 inline-flex items-center justify-center transition-colors " +
      "data-[state=checked]:bg-emerald-500 data-[state=checked]:border-emerald-500 data-[state=checked]:text-white " +
      "data-[state=unchecked]:bg-white dark:data-[state=unchecked]:bg-gray-900",
    label: "text-sm font-medium text-gray-800 dark:text-gray-200",
    description: "text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400",
  }}
/>
```

---

### Patterns

#### Indeterminate "Select All"

```tsx
const [items, setItems] = useState([false, false, false]);
const allChecked = items.every(Boolean);
const someChecked = items.some(Boolean);

<Checkbox
  label="Select All"
  checked={allChecked}
  indeterminate={someChecked && !allChecked}
  onCheckedChange={(checked) => setItems(items.map(() => checked))}
/>
{items.map((checked, i) => (
  <Checkbox
    key={i}
    label={`Item ${i + 1}`}
    checked={checked}
    onCheckedChange={(v) => {
      const next = [...items];
      next[i] = v;
      setItems(next);
    }}
  />
))}
```

#### Form integration

```tsx
<Checkbox
  name="terms"
  required
  error={!!errors.terms}
  errorMessage={errors.terms}
  label="I accept the Terms of Service"
  checked={accepted}
  onCheckedChange={setAccepted}
/>
```

#### Custom icons

```tsx
<Checkbox
  checkedIcon={<HeartIcon className="w-3 h-3 text-pink-500" />}
  uncheckedIcon={<HeartOutlineIcon className="w-3 h-3 text-gray-400" />}
/>
```

---

### Forms

- **Submitted value.** With `name`, it submits `value` (default `"on"`) when checked, and nothing when unchecked — the input is native.
- **Reset.** A form reset — a `type="reset"` button or `form.reset()` — restores an uncontrolled checkbox to `defaultChecked`, on screen as well as in the submitted value, and the submitted value with it. Like a native input it fires no change callback: `onCheckedChange` is not called. A controlled Checkbox is left alone: it keeps the `checked` you pass and calls nothing, as a controlled React `<input>` does. Reset your own state in the form's `onReset` if you want the field cleared.
- **Required.** A `required` Checkbox must be checked: unchecked, it blocks the form's submit and the browser focuses it. The field shows an error state only when you pass `error` and `errorMessage`.

### Keyboard Interactions

A native `<input type="checkbox">`, so the browser owns this — `Enter` deliberately does nothing, as it does not on any checkbox.

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the checkbox. |
| `Space` | Toggles it, including out of the indeterminate state. |

---

---

## CountryFlag

> Renders a country flag image from a two-letter ISO country code. Supports sizes, tooltips, grouping, shimmer loading, and error fallback.

**Category:** Display
**Keywords:** country flag, flag icon, iso code, country, flag image, flag group, locale

### Import

```tsx
import { CountryFlag, CountryFlagGroup, CountryFlagShimmer } from "@chumlab/ui/country-flag";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { CountryFlag, CountryFlagGroup } from "@chumlab/ui/country-flag";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: "flex", gap: 16, alignItems: "center" }}>
      <CountryFlag code="us" size="lg" />
      <CountryFlagGroup maxVisible={3} size="lg">
        <CountryFlag code="gb" />
        <CountryFlag code="jp" />
        <CountryFlag code="de" />
        <CountryFlag code="fr" />
      </CountryFlagGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `code` | Must be a valid two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (lowercase). Invalid codes show fallback. |
| `size` | Preset string (`"xs"` to `"2xl"`) or pixel number. |
| `basePath` | Omit to use the flags packaged with the library (no network request). Set it to load `{basePath}/{code}.svg` from a CDN or self-hosted directory instead. |
| `tooltip` | Pass `ReactNode` for simple tooltip, or `CountryFlagTooltipConfig` object for full control. |

---

### Data Attributes

- `data-code` on root — the normalised alpha-2 code the flag resolved to, so a
  stylesheet can reach one country.
- `data-loading="true"` on root — while the image has not resolved and no
  fallback is showing. It is absent once the flag has loaded.
- `data-error="true"` on root — when the image failed to load
- `role="img"` on root — with `aria-label` set to alt or code

DOM nesting: `root(span) > img + fallback`

---

### Flag assets

The SVGs ship inside the package. By default a `CountryFlag` makes **no network
request** — the flag for a given code is lazily imported as its own chunk, so a
bundle only carries the flags it actually renders, and the component works
offline and in air-gapped installs. Nothing needs to be copied into `public/`.

To serve flags yourself instead — a CDN, or a directory you control — pass
`basePath`, which restores URL-based loading of `{basePath}/{code}.svg`:

```tsx
import { CountryFlag, CHUMLAB_FLAG_CDN } from "@chumlab/ui/country-flag";

<CountryFlag code="in" />                        {/* packaged, no network */}
<CountryFlag code="in" basePath="/flags" />      {/* your own directory */}
<CountryFlag code="in" basePath={CHUMLAB_FLAG_CDN} /> {/* Chumlab's CDN */}
```

The flag renders as an `<img>` in every mode, so `classes.image`, `onLoad`,
`onError` and sizing behave identically whichever you pick.

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from CountryFlag.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `code` **(required)** | string | — | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. 'US', 'GB'). |
| `size` | `"xs"` \| `"sm"` \| `"md"` \| `"lg"` \| `"xl"` \| `"2xl"` \| number | — | Flag size as a preset or numeric pixel value. |
| `aspectRatio` | number | `0.75` | Aspect ratio for the flag image. |
| `alt` | string | — | Alt text for the flag image. |
| `fallback` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom fallback content when the flag image fails to load. |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Shows a loading shimmer placeholder. |
| `tooltip` | object | — | Tooltip shown on hover. Pass a ReactNode or a config object. |
| `basePath` | string | — | Where to load the flag SVG from. Omit to use the flags packaged with the library (no network request). Set it to fetch `${basePath}/${code}.svg` from a CDN or self-hosted directory instead. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for flag sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling. |
| `reduceMotion` | boolean \| `"auto"` | `"auto"` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects OS setting. |
| `onLoad` | object | — | (event: SyntheticEvent<HTMLImageElement>) => void — Fires when the flag image loads. |
| `onError` | object | — | (event: SyntheticEvent<HTMLImageElement>) => void — Fires when the flag image fails to load. |

### Sub-component Props

Generated from the types by `scripts/build-subcomponent-schemas.mjs`.

#### CountryFlagGroup

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Content rendered inside this element. |
| `maxVisible` | `number \| undefined` | How many flags to show before the rest are collapsed into a surplus count. |
| `size` | `number \| CountryFlagSize \| undefined` | Flag size for every member of the group. |
| `showCountTooltip` | `boolean \| undefined` | Shows a tooltip on the surplus count listing the hidden countries. |
| `countTooltip` | `Omit<CountryFlagTooltipConfig, "content"> \| undefined` | Tooltip settings for the surplus count. Its content comes from `surplusTooltipContent`. |
| `surplusTooltipContent` | `ReactNode` | Content for the surplus count's tooltip, replacing the generated country list. |
| `renderSurplus` | `((count: number) => ReactNode) \| undefined` | Renders the surplus indicator yourself, given the number of hidden flags. |
| `classes` | `CountryFlagGroupClasses \| undefined` | Class overrides for this component's slots. |
| `unstyled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Drops the decorative default classes and keeps the structural ones, along with focus, keyboard and ARIA wiring. |

#### CountryFlagShimmer

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classes` | `CountryFlagShimmerClasses \| undefined` | Class overrides for this component's slots. |
| `unstyled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Drops the decorative default classes and keeps the structural ones, along with focus, keyboard and ARIA wiring. |
| `size` | `number \| CountryFlagSize \| undefined` | Matches the flag size the placeholder stands in for. |
| `aspectRatio` | `number \| undefined` | Width-to-height ratio of the placeholder, matching the flag it stands in for. |
| `animate` | `boolean \| undefined` | Whether the placeholder pulses. Set false for a still skeleton. |
| `reduceMotion` | `boolean \| "auto" \| undefined` | Whether to stop the shimmer animation. `"auto"` follows the OS reduced-motion setting. |

#### CountryFlagGroupShimmer

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `number \| undefined` | How many placeholder flags to draw. |
| `size` | `number \| CountryFlagSize \| undefined` | Matches the flag size the placeholder stands in for. |
| `aspectRatio` | `number \| undefined` | Width-to-height ratio of each placeholder. |
| `animate` | `boolean \| undefined` | Whether the placeholders pulse. Set false for a still skeleton. |
| `reduceMotion` | `boolean \| "auto" \| undefined` | Whether to stop the shimmer animation. `"auto"` follows the OS reduced-motion setting. |
| `showCount` | `boolean \| undefined` | Also draws a placeholder for the surplus count. |

---

### Class overrides

#### Slot → element

| Slot | Element |
|------|---------|
| `root` | The element the flag sits in, which carries the size and the hairline border. |
| `image` | The flag graphic. |
| `fallback` | What is shown when the code has no flag, or the image fails. |
| `loading` | The skeleton's bag — `CountryFlagShimmer` is a component, and this is what it paints. |

`CountryFlagGroup` has its own map: `root` (the overlapping row), `item` (each
flag, where the stack margin lives) and `count` (the `+N` disc closing the row).
`CountryFlagShimmer` has `root`.

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** — uses `DEFAULT_COUNTRYFLAG_CLASSES` (layout + overflow)
2. **Partial override** — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** — all slots empty

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root (span, role="img")
├── image (img)
└── fallback (when error)
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot | Notes |
|------------------------|------|-------|
| Flag border/rounding | `root` | Add `rounded-sm border` |
| Image fit | `image` | Default `object-cover` |
| Error fallback | `fallback` | Render custom element via prop |

#### Dark mode

CountryFlag is image-based — no dark mode classes needed. Group count uses `bg-gray-100 text-gray-500` which may need dark variants if overriding.

---

### Patterns

#### Flag group with overflow

```tsx
<CountryFlagGroup maxVisible={3} size="md">
  <CountryFlag code="us" />
  <CountryFlag code="gb" />
  <CountryFlag code="de" />
  <CountryFlag code="fr" />
  <CountryFlag code="jp" />
</CountryFlagGroup>
```

#### With tooltip

```tsx
<CountryFlag code="us" tooltip="United States" size="lg" />
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

Presentational: it renders an image and takes no keyboard input.
