---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

Each variant has its own class slots. Circular: `root`, `control`, `track`, `range`. Linear: `root`, `range`. Dot: `root`, `range`. Pulse: `root`, `range`.

#### CSS custom properties

`CircularLoader` sets three on its root, and its own classes read them, so a
consumer can retune it from a stylesheet without passing props:

| Variable | Set from | Used by |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--loader-size` | `size` | the root's width and height |
| `--loader-duration` | `animationDuration` | the spin's `animation-duration` |
| `--loader-track` | `trackColor` | the track circle's stroke |

#### `size` is a raw pixel number, and the spin is wider than it

There is no size scale and no maximum: `size` is whatever number you pass, 20
by default. One thing it does not tell you — the SVG carries `animate-spin`, so
its **bounding box sweeps out the square's diagonal** while it turns. At
`size={48}` the measured box reaches 67px against a 48px parent, about 41%
wider. The painted circle stays inside `size`; it is layout measurement and hit
testing that see the larger box. `e2e/icon-bounds.spec.ts` names `Loader/sized`
as its one exemption for exactly this reason.

---

### Keyboard Interactions

Presentational: a loader is `role="status"` and takes no keyboard input.

---

---

## Modal

> Accessible dialog overlay with focus trapping, scroll lock, nested modals, animations, and full keyboard navigation.

**Category:** Overlay
**Keywords:** modal, dialog, popup, overlay, lightbox, confirmation, alert dialog, focus trap, scroll lock, nested modal

### Import

```tsx
import { Modal, useModal } from "@chumlab/ui/modal";
import type { ModalProps, ModalClasses } from "@chumlab/ui/modal";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Modal, ModalHeader, ModalBody, ModalFooter } from "@chumlab/ui/modal";
import { Button } from "@chumlab/ui/button";

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open Modal</Button>
      <Modal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <ModalHeader>Welcome Back</ModalHeader>
        <ModalBody>
          <p>Your session has been restored.</p>
        </ModalBody>
        <ModalFooter>
          <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
          <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Continue</Button>
        </ModalFooter>
      </Modal>
    </>
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `open` + `onOpenChange` | Controlled mode — both needed together. |
| `defaultOpen` | Uncontrolled mode — do not combine with `open`. |
| `nestingLevel` | For stacked modals. Auto-managed via context; set manually only for external nesting. |
| `maxNestingLevel` | Prevents infinite nesting. Default: `5`. Exceeding logs a warning in dev. |
| `trapFocus` | Default `true`. Set `false` only for non-modal dialogs. |
| `fullScreen` | Overrides maxWidth/maxHeight. Sets `w-full h-full` on content. |
| `closeOnOverlayClick={false}` + `closeOnEscape={false}` | Combine for mandatory action modals. Must provide explicit close buttons. |
| `showHeader={false}` | Hides title, description, and close button. Must provide your own close mechanism. |
| `keepMounted` | Content stays in DOM when closed. Useful for preserving form state. |
| `initialFocus` | Requires a `RefObject<HTMLElement>`. Focus is set after a 10ms delay. |
| `unstyled` | Strips all default classes. Must provide full styling via `classes`. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

**Root (`data-modal-root`):**
- `data-open` — `true` when modal is visible
- `data-nesting-level` — current nesting depth (0-based)
- `data-reduce-motion` — `true` when reduced motion is active

**Other elements:**
- `data-modal-overlay` — backdrop element
- `data-modal-container` — scroll/centering wrapper; it carries `data-centered` when `centered`
- `data-modal-content` — the `role="dialog"` panel; it carries `data-fullscreen` when `fullScreen`
- `data-modal-header` — header section
- `data-modal-body` — body content area
- `data-modal-footer` — footer (when using `ModalFooter` sub-component)

DOM nesting: `root > overlay + container > content(role="dialog") > header(icon + title + description + closeButton) + body`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from Modal.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `open` | boolean | — | Whether the modal is visible (controlled). |
| `onOpenChange` | object | — | (open: boolean) => void - Callback when the modal's open state changes. |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Whether the modal is initially open (uncontrolled). |
| `children` **(required)** | object | — | React.ReactNode - Modal body content. Use ModalHeader, ModalBody, ModalFooter for structure. |
| `title` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Title rendered in the modal header. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Description rendered below the title in the header. |
| `icon` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Icon rendered in the modal header. |
| `showIcon` | boolean | `false` | Whether to display the icon in the header. |
| `showCloseButton` | boolean | `true` | Whether to display the close button. |
| `closeIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Custom close button icon. |
| `showHeader` | boolean | `true` | Whether to render the built-in header section. |
| `showOverlay` | boolean | `true` | Whether to render the backdrop overlay. |
| `closeOnOverlayClick` | boolean | `true` | Closes the modal when the overlay is clicked. `false` keeps it open until an explicit action. |
| `closeOnEscape` | boolean | `true` | Enables closing via the Escape key. |
| `lockScroll` | boolean | `true` | Locks body scroll when the modal is open. |
| `trapFocus` | boolean | `true` | Traps keyboard focus within the modal. |
| `restoreFocus` | boolean | `true` | Restores focus to the previously focused element on close. |
| `initialFocus` | object | — | RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> - Element to focus when the modal opens. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Keeps the modal DOM mounted when closed. |
| `maxWidth` | string \| number | — | Maximum width of the modal dialog. |
| `maxHeight` | string \| number | — | Maximum height of the modal dialog. |
| `minWidth` | string \| number | — | Minimum width of the modal dialog. |
| `minHeight` | string \| number | — | Minimum height of the modal dialog. |
| `fullScreen` | boolean | `false` | Expands the modal to fill the viewport. |
| `centered` | boolean | `true` | Vertically centers the modal in the viewport. |
| `overlayColor` | string | `"black"` | Custom overlay background color. |
| `overlayOpacity` | number | `0.32` | How strongly `overlayColor` tints the page (0-1), applied as the background's alpha; the overlay element stays opaque so its blur is not diluted. |
| `animationDuration` | number | `200` | Open/close animation duration in milliseconds. |
| `reduceMotion` | boolean \| string | `"auto"` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects the user's OS setting. |
| `nestingLevel` | number | — | Current nesting depth for stacked modals. Managed automatically. |
| `maxNestingLevel` | number | `5` | Maximum allowed nesting depth for stacked modals. |
| `zIndex` | number | — | CSS z-index for the modal layer. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for modal sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling, rendering a plain dialog. |
| `className` | string | `""` | Additional classes for the root, the outer fixed layer, with `classes.root`. Style the dialog surface with `classes.content`. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the root, the outer fixed layer. |
| `contentStyle` | object | — | Inline styles for the dialog content panel. |
| `id` | string | — | The dialog element's id. |
| `aria-label` | string | — | Accessible label for the modal dialog. |
| `aria-labelledby` | string | — | ID of the element that labels the modal dialog. |
| `aria-describedby` | string | — | ID of the element that describes the modal dialog. |

### Ref API

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import { Modal } from "@chumlab/ui/modal";

const modalRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

// Focus the modal content programmatically
modalRef.current?.focus();

<Modal ref={modalRef} open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Title">
  ...
</Modal>
```

---

### Sub-component Props

Generated from the types by `scripts/build-subcomponent-schemas.mjs`.

#### ModalHeader

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Content rendered inside this element. |
| `className` | `string \| undefined` | Additional classes for the root element. |

#### ModalBody

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Content rendered inside this element. |
| `className` | `string \| undefined` | Additional classes for the root element. |

#### ModalFooter

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Content rendered inside this element. |
| `className` | `string \| undefined` | Additional classes for the root element. |

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** (no `classes`, no `unstyled`) — uses `DEFAULT_MODAL_CLASSES`
2. **Partial override** (`classes` without `unstyled`) — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.
3. **Unstyled** (`unstyled={true}`) — all slots empty, you provide everything via `classes`

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root (fixed inset-0, z-50, flex center)
├── overlay (fixed inset-0, bg-black/60, backdrop-blur)
└── positioner (fixed inset-0, overflow-y-auto, flex center, p-4)
    └── content (role="dialog", w-full max-w-lg, rounded-xl, shadow, bg-white dark:bg-gray-800)
        ├── header (flex items-start gap-3, p-6 pb-4)
        │   ├── icon (shrink-0)
        │   ├── div (flex-1)
        │   │   ├── title (font-semibold text-lg)
        │   │   └── description (text-sm text-gray-600)
        │   └── closeTrigger (shrink-0, aria-label="Close modal")
        │       └── closeIcon (w-5 h-5)
        └── body (px-6 pb-6)
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------|-------|
| Root fixed wrapper | `root` | Positioning layer |
| Backdrop color/blur | `overlay` | Also see `overlayColor`/`overlayOpacity` props |
| Scroll/centering wrapper | `positioner` | Controls modal placement |
| Dialog panel | `content` | The visible card |
| Header layout | `header` | Contains icon, title, close button |
| Title text | `title` | |
| Subtitle text | `description` | |
| Header icon | `icon` | Requires `showIcon` |
| Close button | `closeTrigger` | |
| Close icon SVG | `closeIcon` | Or use `closeIcon` prop for custom element |
| Body area | `body` | Where `children` render |

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix, activated by `<html class="dark">`. Content: `bg-white dark:bg-gray-800`. Title: `text-gray-900 dark:text-white`. When overriding slots, always provide both variants.

#### Styling via data attributes

```css
/* Target open state */
[data-modal-root][data-open] { /* ... */ }

/* Target nesting level */
[data-nesting-level="1"] [data-modal-content] { transform: scale(0.95); }
```

#### Complete themed example

```tsx
<Modal
  unstyled
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Custom Modal"
  classes={{
    root: "fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center",
    overlay: "fixed inset-0 bg-black/40 backdrop-blur-sm",
    positioner: "relative z-10 flex items-center justify-center p-4",
    content: "w-full max-w-md rounded-2xl shadow-2xl bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700",
    header: "flex items-start gap-3 p-5 pb-3",
    title: "font-bold text-lg text-gray-900 dark:text-white",
    description: "mt-1 text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400",
    closeTrigger: "shrink-0 p-1.5 rounded-lg ml-auto hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-800",
    closeIcon: "w-5 h-5 text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400",
    body: "px-5 pb-5",
  }}
>
  <p>Fully custom styled modal.</p>
</Modal>
```

---

### Patterns

#### Confirmation dialog

```tsx
<Modal
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Delete project?"
  closeOnOverlayClick={false}
  closeOnEscape={false}
  showCloseButton={false}
>
  <p>This action cannot be undone.</p>
  <div style={{ display: "flex", justifyContent: "flex-end", gap: 8, marginTop: 16 }}>
    <button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</button>
    <button onClick={handleDelete}>Delete</button>
  </div>
</Modal>
```

#### Nested modals

```tsx
<Modal open={level1Open} onOpenChange={setLevel1Open} title="Settings">
  <button onClick={() => setLevel2Open(true)}>Manage Team</button>
  <Modal open={level2Open} onOpenChange={setLevel2Open} title="Team" nestingLevel={1}>
    <p>Nested modal content</p>
  </Modal>
</Modal>
```

#### useModal hook in child components

```tsx
function ModalChild() {
  const { close, nestingLevel } = useModal();
  return <button onClick={close}>Close from child</button>;
}
```

#### Full-screen document viewer

```tsx
<Modal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} showHeader={false} fullScreen centered={false}>
  <div style={{ height: "100%", display: "flex", flexDirection: "column" }}>
    <header>Document title</header>
    <main style={{ flex: 1, overflow: "auto" }}>Content</main>
  </div>
</Modal>
```

#### Form modal with initial focus

```tsx
const emailRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
<Modal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Sign Up" initialFocus={emailRef}>
  <input ref={emailRef} type="email" placeholder="Email" />
</Modal>
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Escape` | Closes the modal, unless `closeOnEscape={false}`. With nesting, only the topmost one closes. |
| `Tab` | Cycles focus inside the dialog while `trapFocus` is on. Focus returns to the trigger on close. |

---

---

## MultiSelectDropdown

> A multi-select dropdown with chip display, checkbox options, async loading, and full style customization.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** multi-select, dropdown, multiselect, checkbox, chips, tags, multiple, select, listbox, combobox, form control

### Import

```tsx
import { MultiSelectDropdown } from "@chumlab/ui/multi-select-dropdown";
import type { MultiSelectOption } from "@chumlab/ui/multi-select-dropdown";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { MultiSelectDropdown } from "@chumlab/ui/multi-select-dropdown";

const options = [
  { value: "apple", label: "Apple" },
  { value: "banana", label: "Banana" },
  { value: "cherry", label: "Cherry" },
];

export default function Example() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([]);
  return (
    <MultiSelectDropdown
      options={options}
      value={selected}
      onValueChange={(values) => setSelected(values)}
      placeholder="Select fruits..."
    />
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `value` + `defaultValue` | Never combine. Use one or the other. |
| `value` requires `onValueChange` | Controlled mode — both needed together. |
| `open` requires `onOpenChange` | Controlled open state — both needed together. |
| `loadOptions` | Requires `loadOnOpen={true}` to trigger. Returns `Promise<MultiSelectOption[]>`. |
| `loadOnOpen` | Only works when `loadOptions` is provided. |
| `forceDropdownSide` | Only meaningful with `dropdownSide`. Disables auto-flip. |
| `lockScroll` | Prevents body scroll while open. Default: `false`. |
| `showSelectedChips` | Default `true`. Set `false` to show count-only display. |
| `maxVisible` | Truncates chips with "+N more" badge. |
| `clearable` | Shows clear button when values are selected. |
| `name` | Renders hidden `<input>` elements for native form submission. |
| `renderTrigger` | `renderTrigger(triggerProps, state)` replaces the default `<button>`. Spread `triggerProps` onto a `<button>`: it is exactly what the default trigger renders, ref and `type="button"` included. Draw from `state` (`isOpen`, `selectedOptions`, `placeholder`), which never reaches the DOM. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

**Root element:**
- `data-disabled` — when `disabled={true}`
- `data-error` — when `error={true}`
- `data-open` — when dropdown is open
- `data-full-width` — when `fullWidth={true}`
- `data-valid` — when `success={true}`

**Trigger element:**
- `data-disabled`, `data-error`, `data-open` — mirrors root
- `data-placeholder` — when no options are selected; the placeholder text is tertiary

**Dropdown panel:**
- `data-position` — `"top"` or `"bottom"` (actual rendered position)
- `data-state="open" | "closed"`
- `data-dropdown-id` — unique ID for click-outside detection
- `data-side` — on the surface, the side it was placed on after any flip

**Options:**
- `data-selected` — a selected option; its checkbox is checked
- `data-highlighted` — the keyboard position
- `data-disabled` — a disabled option

**Option checkbox:** `data-state="checked" | "unchecked"`, and `data-checked` while checked

**Messages:** `data-invalid` on the error message

DOM nesting: `root > label + description + wrapper > trigger(combobox) + content(portal) > optionList(listbox) > options`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from MultiSelectDropdown.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | array | `[]` | List of selectable options. |
| `value` | array | — | Controlled selected values. |
| `defaultValue` | array | — | Initial selected values for uncontrolled usage. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (values: string[], options: MultiSelectOption[]) => void - Fires when the selected values change. |
| `id` | string | — | HTML id attribute for the trigger element. |
| `name` | string | — | Form field name. |
| `placeholder` | object | `"Select options..."` | React.ReactNode - Placeholder when nothing is selected. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables the dropdown. |
| `error` | boolean | `false` | Displays the dropdown in an error state. |
| `errorMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Error message displayed below the dropdown. |
| `label` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Label rendered above the dropdown. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Description text rendered below the label. |
| `success` | boolean | `false` | Displays the dropdown in a success state. |
| `successMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Success message displayed below the dropdown. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Marks the field as required. |
| `emptyContent` | object | `"No options found"` | React.ReactNode - Content shown when no options are available. |
| `clearable` | boolean | `false` | Shows a clear button to deselect all values. |
| `showChevron` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show the chevron icon in the trigger. |
| `fullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Makes the dropdown span the full width of its container. |
| `loading` | boolean | — | Shows a loading/shimmer state. |
| `loadOptions` | object | — | () => Promise<MultiSelectOption[]> - Async function to load options. Requires `loadOnOpen`; alone it never fires. |
| `loadOnOpen` | boolean | `false` | When true, calls loadOptions each time the dropdown opens. Requires `loadOptions`; alone it has nothing to load. |
| `onLoadError` | object | — | (error: unknown) => void - Called when async option loading fails. |
| `shimmerCount` | number | `5` | Number of shimmer placeholder items shown during loading. |
| `maxVisible` | number | `3` | Maximum number of selected chips displayed before showing a count. The chip strip WRAPS and does not clip: with this cap the strip cannot overflow, so clipping it bought nothing and cost hit area — a 24px remove target inside a 20px clipped row is only 24x20 to a pointer. Decided 2026-09-11; the two components diverged silently before that. |
| `showSelectedChips` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show selected values as chips in the trigger. |
| `checkboxIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Custom checkbox icon for options. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling. |
| `lockScroll` | boolean | `false` | Locks body scroll while the dropdown is open. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for dropdown sub-elements. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional CSS class for the root element. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the root element. |
| `open` | boolean | — | Controlled open state. |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Whether the dropdown is initially open (uncontrolled). |
| `onOpenChange` | object | — | (open: boolean) => void - Fires when the open state changes. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Keeps the dropdown DOM mounted when closed. |
| `portalContainer` | object | — | HTMLElement \| null - Portal target for the dropdown popup. |
| `dropdownSide` | `"top"` \| `"bottom"` | `"bottom"` | Vertical placement of the dropdown relative to the trigger. |
| `forceDropdownSide` | boolean | `false` | Locks the dropdown to the specified position without auto-flipping. |
| `dropdownZIndex` | number | `50` | Z-index of the dropdown popup. |
| `dropdownOffset` | number | `4` | Gap in pixels between trigger and dropdown popup. |
| `typeaheadTimeout` | number | `500` | Timeout in milliseconds for keyboard typeahead matching. |
| `aria-label` | string | — | Accessible label for the dropdown. |
| `aria-labelledby` | string | — | Names the field by another element, and wins over `label` and `aria-label`. Lands on the trigger. |
| `aria-describedby` | string | — | Lands on the trigger, joined with the component's own error message. |
| `onBlur` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void - Fires when the trigger loses focus, with the native focus event. |
| `onFocus` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void - Fires when the trigger takes focus, with the native focus event. |
| `onKeyDown` | object | — | (event: React.KeyboardEvent) => void - Fires on keydown events. |
| `chevronIcon` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the trigger's chevron. Rendered inside a box carrying `classes.icon`, which turns it over while the menu is open. |
| `loadingContent` | object | `"Loading..."` | React.ReactNode - Text shown during async loading. |
| `clearIcon` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the clear button's glyph. Rendered as given. |
| `renderTrigger` | object | — | (triggerProps: MultiSelectDropdownTriggerRenderProps, state: MultiSelectDropdownTriggerState) => ReactNode - Custom render function for the trigger element. Spread triggerProps onto a <button>; draw from state (isOpen, selectedOptions, placeholder). |

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** (no `classes`, no `unstyled`) — uses `DEFAULT_MULTISELECTDROPDOWN_CLASSES`
2. **Partial override** (`classes` without `unstyled`) — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** (`unstyled={true}`) — all slots empty, you provide everything

```tsx
// `item` carries the base AND 3 state variants. Overriding it
// replaces all of them, so write them together:
<MultiSelectDropdown
  classes={{
    item:
      "rounded-cl-md px-2 py-1 " +           // base
      "data-[disabled]:opacity-50 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed " +
      "data-[highlighted]:bg-cl-bg-hover " +
      "data-[selected]:bg-cl-accent/15 data-[selected]:text-cl-accent ",
  }}
/>

// Passing only `item: "data-[disabled]:…"` drops the base and the other
// 2 states.
```

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root
├── label
├── description
└── control
    └── trigger (role="combobox")
    │   ├── chips (chip + chipRemoveTrigger) or value
    │   ├── count (+N more)
    │   ├── clearTrigger
    │   └── icon
    └── content (portal)
        └── list (role="listbox")
            └── item (itemControl + itemIndicator + label)
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------|-------|
| Trigger button | `trigger` | Contains chips/text |
| Selected chips | `chip`, `chipRemoveTrigger` | Individual chip + X button |
| Dropdown panel | `content` | Portal-rendered |
| Option row | `item` | |
| Checkbox | `itemControl`, `itemIndicator` | |
| Chevron icon | `icon` | |
| "+N more" badge | `count` | |

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix. When overriding, always provide both light and dark variants.

---

### Patterns

#### Controlled multi-select

```tsx
const [values, setValues] = useState<string[]>([]);
<MultiSelectDropdown
  options={options}
  value={values}
  onValueChange={(v) => setValues(v)}
  placeholder="Select..."
/>
```

#### Async loading on open

```tsx
<MultiSelectDropdown
  loadOnOpen
  loadOptions={() => fetch("/api/options").then(r => r.json())}
  placeholder="Click to load..."
/>
```

#### Force dropdown position

```tsx
<MultiSelectDropdown
  options={options}
  dropdownSide="top"
  forceDropdownSide
  lockScroll
/>
```

---

### Forms

- **Submitted value.** With `name`, it submits one entry per selected value under that name, in option order (`a`, then `c`), as a native `<select multiple>` does, and nothing when none is selected. Read them with `FormData.getAll(name)`: a value containing a comma comes back whole.
- **Reset.** A form reset — a `type="reset"` button or `form.reset()` — restores an uncontrolled selection to `defaultValue` (or no selection), and the submitted value with it. Like a native input it fires no change callback: `onValueChange` is not called. A controlled MultiSelectDropdown is left alone: it keeps the `value` you pass and calls nothing, as a controlled React `<input>` does. Reset your own state in the form's `onReset` if you want the field cleared.
- **Required.** A `required` MultiSelectDropdown needs at least one value: with none, it blocks the form's submit and the browser's validation moves focus to the trigger. The field shows an error state only when you pass `error` and `errorMessage`.
- **Disabled.** A disabled MultiSelectDropdown submits nothing, as a disabled native control doesn't.

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Enter`, `Space` | Opens the menu, and toggles the focused option without closing it. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | Moves between options. `aria-activedescendant` on the trigger follows, so focus itself never leaves it. |
| `Home`, `End` | Jumps to the first or last option. |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. Always: there is no prop to turn it off, because the APG combobox pattern requires Escape to close the popup. |
| `Tab` | Closes the menu and moves focus on. |

---

### Ref API

The ref lands on the trigger, the `<button role="combobox">` a keyboard user tabs to, so `ref.current.focus()` focuses the field — which is what a form library calls on the first invalid field. With `renderTrigger`, it is the element your trigger attaches `triggerProps.ref` to.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
<MultiSelectDropdown ref={ref} options={options} />
// ref.current is the trigger <button>
```

### Selected-chip strip

The strip **wraps**; it does not clip. `maxVisible` (default 3) caps how
many chips render and the rest collapse into a count, so the strip cannot
overflow its trigger and there is nothing for a clip to protect against.

This is recorded because it was not decided once. `MultiSelectDropdown` shipped
`overflow: hidden` with `flex-wrap: nowrap` while `MultiSelectSearchableDropdown`
shipped `flex-wrap`, both introduced in the same commit — one titled for
unrelated Accordion work — and nothing in either component, schema or document
said which was intended. The clip also cost hit area: the remove control is 24px
via a negative margin inside a 20px row, so the clip took 4px out of the target a
pointer can reach while `target-size` still read 24x24 from the rect.

---

## MultiSelectSearchableDropdown

> A multi-select dropdown with built-in search, chip display, async search/prefetch, checkbox options, and full style customization.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** multi-select, searchable, dropdown, multiselect, search, filter, checkbox, chips, tags, async, combobox, form control

### Import

```tsx
import { MultiSelectSearchableDropdown } from "@chumlab/ui/multi-select-searchable-dropdown";
import type { MultiSelectOption } from "@chumlab/ui/multi-select-searchable-dropdown";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { MultiSelectSearchableDropdown } from "@chumlab/ui/multi-select-searchable-dropdown";

const options = [
  { value: "apple", label: "Apple" },
  { value: "banana", label: "Banana" },
  { value: "cherry", label: "Cherry" },
];

export default function Example() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([]);
  return (
    <MultiSelectSearchableDropdown
      options={options}
      value={selected}
      onValueChange={(values) => setSelected(values)}
      placeholder="Search and select..."
    />
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `value` + `defaultValue` | Never combine. Use one or the other. |
| `value` requires `onValueChange` | Controlled mode — both needed together. |
| `open` requires `onOpenChange` | Controlled open state — both needed together. |
| `searchOptions` | Async search function. Replaces local filtering when provided. |
| `loadInitialOptions` | Requires `loadInitialOnOpen={true}` to trigger on open. |
| `searchDebounce` | Only applies to `searchOptions`. Default: `300`. |
| `showSearch` | Default `true`. Set `false` to hide search input. |
| `forceDropdownSide` | Only meaningful with `dropdownSide`. Disables auto-flip. |
| `lockScroll` | Prevents body scroll while open. Default: `false`. |
| `showSelectedChips` | Default `true`. Set `false` for count-only display. |
| `maxVisible` | Truncates chips with "+N more" badge. |
| `name` | Renders hidden inputs for form submission. |
| `renderTrigger` | `renderTrigger(triggerProps, state)` replaces the default `<button>`. Spread `triggerProps` onto a `<button>`: it is exactly what the default trigger renders, ref and `type="button"` included. Draw from `state` (`isOpen`, `selectedOptions`, `placeholder`), which never reaches the DOM. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

**Root element:**
- `data-disabled`, `data-error`, `data-open`, `data-full-width`, `data-valid`

**Trigger element:**
- `data-disabled`, `data-error`, `data-open`
- `data-placeholder` — when no options are selected; the placeholder text is tertiary

**Dropdown panel:**
- `data-position` — `"top"` or `"bottom"`
- `data-state="open" | "closed"`
- `data-dropdown-id` — unique ID for click-outside detection
- `data-side` — on the surface, the side it was placed on after any flip

**Options:**
- `data-selected` — a selected option; its checkbox is checked
- `data-highlighted` — the keyboard position
- `data-disabled` — a disabled option

**Option checkbox:** `data-state="checked" | "unchecked"`, and `data-checked` while checked

**Messages:** `data-invalid` on the error message

DOM nesting: `root > label + description + wrapper > trigger(combobox) + content(portal) > searchInput + optionList(listbox) > options`

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** — uses `DEFAULT_MULTISELECTSEARCHABLEDROPDOWN_CLASSES`
2. **Partial override** — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** — all slots empty, you build from scratch

```tsx
// `item` carries the base AND 3 state variants. Overriding it
// replaces all of them, so write them together:
<MultiSelectSearchableDropdown
  classes={{
    item:
      "rounded-cl-md px-2 py-1 " +           // base
      "data-[disabled]:opacity-50 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed " +
      "data-[highlighted]:bg-cl-bg-hover " +
      "data-[selected]:bg-cl-accent/15 data-[selected]:text-cl-accent ",
  }}
/>

// Passing only `item: "data-[disabled]:…"` drops the base and the other
// 2 states.
```

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root
├── label
├── description
└── control
    └── trigger (role="combobox")
    │   ├── chips / value / count
    │   ├── clearTrigger
    │   └── icon
    └── content (portal)
        ├── searchControl > searchIcon + searchInput
        └── list (role="listbox")
            └── item (itemControl + itemIndicator + label)
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Search input wrapper | `searchControl` |
| Search text input | `searchInput` |
| Search icon | `searchIcon` |
| Loading indicator | `loading` |
| Everything else | Same as MultiSelectDropdown |

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix. When overriding, provide both light and dark variants.

---

### Patterns

#### Async search with API

```tsx
<MultiSelectSearchableDropdown
  searchOptions={async (query) => {
    const res = await fetch(`/api/search?q=${query}`);
    return res.json();
  }}
  searchDebounce={300}
  placeholder="Search..."
/>
```

#### Prefetch on open + async search

```tsx
<MultiSelectSearchableDropdown
  loadInitialOnOpen
  loadInitialOptions={() => fetch("/api/popular").then(r => r.json())}
  searchOptions={(q) => fetch(`/api/search?q=${q}`).then(r => r.json())}
/>
```

#### Force dropdown position

```tsx
<MultiSelectSearchableDropdown
  options={options}
  dropdownSide="top"
  forceDropdownSide
  lockScroll
/>
```

---

### Forms

- **Submitted value.** With `name`, it submits one entry per selected value under that name, in option order (`a`, then `c`), as a native `<select multiple>` does, and nothing when none is selected. Read them with `FormData.getAll(name)`: a value containing a comma comes back whole.
- **Reset.** A form reset — a `type="reset"` button or `form.reset()` — restores an uncontrolled selection to `defaultValue` (or no selection), and the submitted value with it. Like a native input it fires no change callback: `onValueChange` is not called. A controlled MultiSelectSearchableDropdown is left alone: it keeps the `value` you pass and calls nothing, as a controlled React `<input>` does. Reset your own state in the form's `onReset` if you want the field cleared.
- **Required.** A `required` MultiSelectSearchableDropdown needs at least one value: with none, it blocks the form's submit and the browser's validation moves focus to the trigger. The field shows an error state only when you pass `error` and `errorMessage`.
- **Disabled.** A disabled MultiSelectSearchableDropdown submits nothing, as a disabled native control doesn't.

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Enter`, `Space` | Opens the menu, and toggles the focused option without closing it. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | Moves between the filtered options. `aria-activedescendant` sits on the search input, which holds focus. |
| `Home`, `End` | Jumps to the first or last filtered option. |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. Always: there is no prop to turn it off, because the APG combobox pattern requires Escape to close the popup. |
| `Tab` | Closes the menu and moves focus on. |
| Printable characters | Types into the search box and filters the list. |

---

### Ref API

The ref lands on the trigger, the `<button role="combobox">` a keyboard user tabs to, so `ref.current.focus()` focuses the field — which is what a form library calls on the first invalid field. With `renderTrigger`, it is the element your trigger attaches `triggerProps.ref` to.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
<MultiSelectSearchableDropdown ref={ref} options={options} />
// ref.current is the trigger <button>
```

### Selected-chip strip

The strip **wraps**; it does not clip. `maxVisible` (default 3) caps how
many chips render and the rest collapse into a count, so the strip cannot
overflow its trigger and there is nothing for a clip to protect against.

This is recorded because it was not decided once. `MultiSelectDropdown` shipped
`overflow: hidden` with `flex-wrap: nowrap` while `MultiSelectSearchableDropdown`
shipped `flex-wrap`, both introduced in the same commit — one titled for
unrelated Accordion work — and nothing in either component, schema or document
said which was intended. The clip also cost hit area: the remove control is 24px
via a negative margin inside a 20px row, so the clip took 4px out of the target a
pointer can reach while `target-size` still read 24x24 from the rect.

---

## OtpInput

> A one-time password input with per-character fields, keyboard navigation, paste support, grouping, and validation.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** otp, one-time password, verification code, pin input, code input, 2fa, mfa

### Import

```tsx
import { OtpInput } from "@chumlab/ui/otp-input";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { OtpInput } from "@chumlab/ui/otp-input";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function Example() {
  const [otp, setOtp] = useState("");
  return (
    <OtpInput
      label="Verification Code"
      description="Enter the 6-digit code sent to your phone"
      value={otp}
      onValueChange={setOtp}
    />
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `length` | Defaults to 6. Controls number of input fields. |
| `inputPattern` | Regex string restricting allowed characters, e.g. `"\\d*"` for digits only. The single source for what a slot accepts: it sets the `pattern` attribute, drives `inputMode`, names the slots "Digit" or "Character", **and filters typed and pasted characters**. |
| `inputType` | `"text"` (default), `"tel"`, or `"password"`. Use `"password"` to mask characters. |
| `groups` | Array like `[3, 3]` to visually group inputs with separators. Sum must equal `length`. |
| `validate` | Custom function `(char) => boolean`. Overrides `inputPattern` filtering. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

Every one of these is written or absent, never `"false"`, so the bare attribute
selector is the one to use: `[data-error]`, not `[data-error="true"]`.

- `data-error="true"` on the root and on each input — when `error={true}`
- `data-disabled="true"` on the root and on each input — when disabled
- `data-loading="true"` on the root — when `loading={true}`
- `data-valid="true"` on the root in the success state, and on the success message
- `data-invalid="true"` on the error message
- `data-index` on each input — its zero-based position, always present
- `data-filled="true"` on an input holding a character
- `data-group` on each group wrapper — the group's zero-based index, only when
  `groups` is set

DOM nesting: `root > label + description + control > (group > input…) + separator + message`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from OtpInput.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `length` | number | `6` | Number of OTP input fields. |
| `value` | string | — | Controlled OTP value. |
| `defaultValue` | string | — | Initial OTP value for uncontrolled usage. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (value: string) => void - Fires when the OTP value changes. |
| `onComplete` | object | — | (value: string) => void - Fires when all fields are filled. |
| `label` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Label rendered above the input. |
| `id` | string | — | HTML id attribute. |
| `name` | string | — | Form field name. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Marks the field as required. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Helper text rendered below the label. |
| `error` | boolean | `false` | Displays the input in an error state. |
| `errorMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Error message displayed below the input. |
| `success` | boolean | `false` | Displays the input in a success state. |
| `successMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Success message displayed below the input. |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Shows a loading state. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables all input fields. |
| `groups` | array | — | Defines grouping of input fields (e.g. [3, 3] for two groups of 3). |
| `separator` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Content rendered between groups. |
| `allowPaste` | boolean | `true` | Enables pasting OTP values. |
| `autoFocusFirst` | boolean | `false` | Automatically focuses the first input on mount. |
| `inputType` | `"text"` \| `"password"` \| `"tel"` | `"text"` | HTML input type for each field. |
| `inputPattern` | string | `"\\d*"` | HTML pattern attribute for input validation. |
| `inputClassNames` | array | — | Per-input CSS class overrides. |
| `fullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Makes the input span the full width of its container. |
| `renderInput` | object | — | (props: OtpInputRenderProps) => ReactNode - Custom render function for individual input fields. |
| `validate` | object | — | (char: string) => boolean - Custom validation function for each character. |
| `inputAriaLabel` | object | — | (index: number, length: number) => string - Function to generate aria-label for each input. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling. |

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

A restyle that drops the box, such as an underline, must also replace the focus ring: pass `focus-visible:ring-0` and mark focus on the edge you keep, or the default `focus-visible:ring-2` survives the merge and each cell focuses as a box.

#### Slot → visual mapping

| Slot | Element |
|------|---------|
| `root` | The field and everything labelling it. |
| `label` | The label above the row. |
| `description` | The helper line under the label. |
| `control` | The row of boxes. |
| `group` | One run of boxes when `groups` splits the code up. |
| `input` | A single character box. |
| `separator` | What is drawn between two groups. |
| `message` | The error or hint line under the row. |

#### The `input` slot carries the error and focus states

The box is painted by one class string holding four variants:
`data-[error]:border-cl-error` for the error state,
`focus-visible:border-cl-border-input-focus` for focus, and
`data-[error]:focus-visible:border-cl-border-input-focus` for **both at once**.
That third one is not redundant. Without it, a focused box in an error state
kept the error border and the focus ring landed on it at **1.30:1** — measured,
and below the 3:1 a focus indicator has to clear.

A plain utility of the same property drops all three, so
`classes={{ input: "border-gray-300" }}` leaves a field with no error border and
no focus indicator. Pass the states you want to keep:

```tsx
<OtpInput
  error
  classes={{
    input:
      "border-gray-300 data-[error]:border-red-600 focus-visible:border-blue-600 data-[error]:focus-visible:border-blue-600",
  }}
/>
```

---

### Changed behaviour

**A default `<OtpInput />` now rejects non-digits.**

`inputPattern` defaults to `"\\d*"` and has always set the `pattern` attribute,
`inputMode="numeric"` and the "Digit N of M" slot labels. It did not filter,
because `pattern` is form-validation metadata that browsers do not apply to
typing — so the component told the browser, the soft keyboard and the screen
reader that it wanted digits, and then accepted letters (E2E-TRIAGE.md). The
filter is now derived from the same pattern, so all four agree.

- **Digits-only consumers:** no change; this is what the labels already claimed.
- **Consumers relying on the permissive default** must now say so, with
  `inputPattern="[\\s\\S]"` or an explicit `validate`.
- **Alphanumeric codes:** `inputPattern="[A-Za-z0-9]"`, which also widens
  `inputMode` to `"text"` and relabels the slots "Character N of M".
- An explicit `validate` still wins outright.
- A pattern that will not compile falls back to accepting everything, matching
  what the browser does with the attribute.

---

### Forms

- **Submitted value.** With `name`, it submits one entry, the digits entered so far, or an empty string.
- **Reset.** A form reset — a `type="reset"` button or `form.reset()` — restores an uncontrolled code to `defaultValue` (or empty), and the submitted value with it. Like a native input it fires no change callback: `onValueChange` is not called. A controlled OtpInput is left alone: it keeps the `value` you pass and calls nothing, as a controlled React `<input>` does. Reset your own state in the form's `onReset` if you want the field cleared.
- **Required.** An empty `required` OtpInput blocks the form's submit, and the browser's validation moves focus to the first digit. A partly filled code counts as filled. The field shows an error state only when you pass `error` and `errorMessage`.
- **Disabled.** A disabled OtpInput submits nothing.

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves to the next box. Every box is in the tab order — there is no roving tabindex, so tabbing out of the field takes as many presses as it has boxes. |
| `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` | Moves between boxes. |
| `Home`, `End` | Jumps to the first or last box. |
| `Backspace` | Clears the current box and steps back. On a box that is already empty it steps back and clears that one instead. |
| `Delete` | Clears the current box without moving. |
| Printable characters | Fills the box and advances. A paste of the full code fills every box at once. |

---

---

## Pagination

> Accessible page navigation with page buttons, rows-per-page selector, custom ellipsis, page info display, section reordering, i18n, and full style customization.

**Category:** Navigation
**Keywords:** pagination, pager, page navigation, rows per page, page selector, data table, ellipsis, page info, i18n

### Import

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@chumlab/ui/pagination";
import type { PaginationProps, PaginationClasses } from "@chumlab/ui/pagination";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Pagination } from "@chumlab/ui/pagination";

export default function Example() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  return <Pagination value={page} totalPages={10} onValueChange={setPage} />;
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `value` + `onValueChange` | Controlled mode — both needed together. |
| `defaultValue` | Uncontrolled mode — do not combine with `value`. |
| `totalPages` | **Required.** Must be >= 0. |
| `showRowsPerPage` | Requires `rowsPerPage` and `onRowsPerPageChange`. |
| `rowOptions` | Only meaningful with `showRowsPerPage`. Default: `[5, 10, 25, 50, 100]`. |
| `sectionOrder` | Controls layout order: `["selector", "pageInfo", "nav"]`. |
| `renderEllipsis` | Replaces default `...` with custom content. Receives `{ position, onValueChange }`. |
| `renderPageInfo` | Custom render for page info. Receives `{ value, totalPages, rowsPerPage }`. |
| `prevIcon` / `nextIcon` / `dropdownIcon` | Elements, not components, rendered as given. `classes.navIcon` styles the default arrows and `classes.rowsPerPage.icon` the default chevron. |
| `dropdownSide` | `"top"` or `"bottom"` — controls rows dropdown direction. |
| `unstyled` | Strips all default classes. Must provide styling via `classes`. |

---

### Narrow containers

Prev, the page list and next always share one row; the list never wraps.
`siblingCount` is the most sibling pages shown. When the row would overflow
the space its host gives it, measured with a `ResizeObserver` on the
component's own `<nav>` and on its host (so a narrow sidebar or a centred
footer counts, not just a narrow window), Pagination steps down, one step per
measurement:

1. Fewer siblings, down to 0: the first page, the current page and the last
   page, with ellipses between.
2. Compact spacing: the list's gap and the ellipsis padding go from 8 px to
   4 px.
3. Compact padding: the page buttons' horizontal padding goes from 12 px to
   8 px, with a 24 px minimum width, so every button keeps at least a
   24 × 24 px target.
4. If that still does not fit, the page list scrolls horizontally inside the
   row; prev and next stay on it, and the current page is scrolled into view.

The `<nav>` never grows past its host. When the host grows, Pagination starts
again from `siblingCount`. The server and the first client render show the
full set, so there is no hydration mismatch; the step-down runs after mount.

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

- `data-disabled` — on prev/next buttons at a boundary, and on every button when `disabled`
- `data-active` — on the active page button
- `data-selected` — on the selected row option in dropdown
- `data-highlighted` — on keyboard-focused dropdown option
- `data-state` — `"open"` on dropdown portal when visible
- `data-direction` — `"up"` or `"down"` on dropdown portal
- `data-side` — on the rows-per-page surface, the side it was placed on after any flip
- `data-reduce-motion` — on the root `<nav>`, while reduced motion is in force
- `aria-current="page"` — on the active page button
- `aria-expanded` — on selector button

DOM nesting: `nav(root) > [selector + pageInfo + nav(reorderable)] > nav > prevButton + pageButtons + ellipsis + nextButton`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from Pagination.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `totalPages` **(required)** | number | — | Total number of pages. |
| `siblingCount` | number | `1` | The most sibling page buttons shown on each side of the current page. When the page row would overflow its container, Pagination shows fewer, down to none, keeping the first, current and last pages with ellipses between; then it tightens the list's spacing; then the page buttons' padding; and if even that does not fit, the page list scrolls inside the row while prev and next stay on it. The server and first render show the full set. |
| `rowsPerPage` | number | — | Current number of rows displayed per page. |
| `rowOptions` | array | — | Available row-per-page options for the selector. |
| `disabled` | boolean | — | Disables the entire pagination control. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (page: number) => void - Fires when the current page changes. |
| `value` | number | — | Controlled current page number. |
| `defaultValue` | number | `1` | Initial page number for uncontrolled usage. |
| `onRowsPerPageChange` | object | — | (rows: number) => void - Fires when the rows-per-page value changes. |
| `showRowsPerPage` | boolean | `false` | Whether to show the rows-per-page selector. |
| `rowsPerPageSuffix` | string | `"rows"` | Visible text after the rows-per-page select ("Show 10 rows"). With the prefix, it names the select; with both empty the select is named "Rows per page". |
| `rowsPerPagePrefix` | string | `"Show"` | Visible text before the rows-per-page select. With the suffix, it names the select; the number is its value. |
| `dropdownAriaLabel` | string | `"Rows per page"` | Accessible label for the rows-per-page dropdown. |
| `dropdownSide` | `"top"` \| `"bottom"` | `"top"` | Vertical placement of the rows-per-page dropdown — opens upward (top) or downward (bottom). |
| `dropdownZIndex` | number | `50` | Z-index of the rows-per-page dropdown. |
| `dropdownOffset` | number | `4` | Gap in pixels between trigger and dropdown. |
| `dropdownIcon` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the rows-per-page select's chevron. Rendered as given; `classes.rowsPerPage.icon` styles the default one. |
| `prevIcon` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the previous-page arrow. Rendered as given; `classes.navIcon` styles the default one. |
| `nextIcon` | object | — | ReactNode — Replaces the next-page arrow. Rendered as given; `classes.navIcon` styles the default one. |
| `renderEllipsis` | object | — | (props: EllipsisRenderProps) => ReactNode - Custom render function for the ellipsis element. |
| `renderPageInfo` | object | — | (props: PageInfoRenderProps) => ReactNode - Custom render function for the page info display. |
| `sectionOrder` | array | — | Order of pagination sections. |
| `reduceMotion` | `true` \| `false` \| `"auto"` | `"auto"` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects the user's OS setting. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for pagination sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling. |
| `portalContainer` | object | — | HTMLElement \| null - Portal target for the rows-per-page dropdown. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Keeps the rows-per-page menu mounted while closed. |
| `prevAriaLabel` | string | `"Previous page"` | Accessible label for the previous page button. |
| `nextAriaLabel` | string | `"Next page"` | Accessible label for the next page button. |
| `paginationAriaLabel` | string | — | Accessible label for the pagination nav element. |
| `pageAriaLabel` | object | — | (page: number) => string - Function to generate aria-label for each page button. |

### Ref API

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import { Pagination } from "@chumlab/ui/pagination";

const paginationRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);

// Focus the row element
paginationRef.current?.focus();

<Pagination ref={paginationRef} value={page} totalPages={10} onValueChange={setPage} />
```

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** (no `classes`, no `unstyled`) — uses `DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASSES`
2. **Partial override** (`classes` without `unstyled`) — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** (`unstyled={true}`) — all slots empty, you provide everything

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root (row, flex flex-wrap)
├── rowsPerPage (rows-per-page)
│   ├── label ("Show")
│   ├── selectorButton (trigger)
│   │   └── dropdownIcon
│   ├── selectorDropdownWrapper (portal)
│   │   └── selectorDropdown
│   │       └── selectorOption (role="option")
│   └── label ("rows")
├── pageInfo (custom render slot)
└── row (navigation controls)
    ├── navTrigger (prev)
    │   └── navIcon
    ├── list
    │   ├── item [data-state=active]
    │   └── ellipsis
    └── navTrigger (next)
        └── navIcon
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------|-------|
| Root layout | `root` | Controls flex direction and gap |
| Page buttons | `item` | Inactive and active styles |
| Prev/next buttons | `navTrigger` | Shared for both |
| Ellipsis dots | `ellipsis` | Or use `renderEllipsis` for custom |
| Rows dropdown trigger | `rowsPerPage.trigger` | |
| Dropdown panel | `rowsPerPage.content` | Portal-rendered |
| Dropdown option | `rowsPerPage.item` | Use `data-[selected]` and `data-[highlighted]` |
| Icons | `navIcon`, `navIcon`, `rowsPerPage.icon` | |

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix. When overriding, always provide both light and dark variants.

#### Complete themed example (Pill style)

```tsx
<Pagination
  value={page}
  totalPages={10}
  onValueChange={setPage}
  classes={{
    root: "flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1",
    navTrigger: "p-2 rounded-full border shadow-sm bg-white border-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 dark:border-gray-600",
    item: "w-9 h-9 rounded-full border shadow-sm flex items-center justify-center text-sm bg-white border-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 dark:border-gray-600 data-[state=active]:shadow-md data-[state=active]:bg-blue-600 data-[state=active]:border-blue-600 data-[state=active]:text-white",
    list: "flex items-center gap-1",
    navIcon: "w-4 h-4",
    ellipsis: "px-2 text-gray-400",
  }}
/>
```

---

### Patterns

#### Data table pagination with rows selector

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
const [rows, setRows] = useState(10);
<Pagination
  value={page}
  totalPages={Math.ceil(totalItems / rows)}
  onValueChange={setPage}
  showRowsPerPage
  rowsPerPage={rows}
  onRowsPerPageChange={(r) => { setRows(r); setPage(1); }}
/>
```

#### Jump-to-page ellipsis

```tsx
<Pagination
  renderEllipsis={({ onValueChange }) => (
    <input
      type="number"
      onKeyDown={(e) => {
        if (e.key === "Enter") onValueChange(Number(e.currentTarget.value));
      }}
    />
  )}
/>
```

#### Page info display

```tsx
<Pagination
  renderPageInfo={({ value, totalPages }) => (
    <span>Page {value} of {totalPages}</span>
  )}
/>
```

#### i18n (French)

```tsx
<Pagination
  rowsPerPagePrefix="Afficher"
  rowsPerPageSuffix="lignes"
  dropdownAriaLabel="Lignes par page"
  paginationAriaLabel="Navigation des pages"
  prevAriaLabel="Page précédente"
  nextAriaLabel="Page suivante"
  pageAriaLabel={(p) => `Page ${p}`}
/>
```

#### Section reordering

```tsx
<Pagination sectionOrder={["row", "pageInfo", "rowsPerPage"]} />
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves between the page buttons, the navigation arrows and the rows-per-page trigger. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Activates the focused control. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | Moves between options in the open rows-per-page menu. |
| `Home`, `End` | Jumps to the first or last option in that menu. |
| `Escape` | Closes it and returns focus to the trigger. Always: there is no prop to turn it off, because the APG combobox pattern requires Escape to close the popup. |

---

---

## RadioButton

> A radio button group with labels, descriptions, custom icons, sizes, orientations, and validation states.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** radio, radio button, radio group, option select, single select, form, choice

### Import

```tsx
import { RadioGroup, RadioButton } from "@chumlab/ui/radio-button";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { RadioGroup, RadioButton } from "@chumlab/ui/radio-button";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <RadioGroup name="plan" defaultValue="basic">
      <RadioButton value="basic" label="Basic" />
      <RadioButton value="pro" label="Pro" />
      <RadioButton value="enterprise" label="Enterprise" />
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from RadioButton.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

#### RadioGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | string | — | Currently selected value. |
| `defaultValue` | string | `""` | Initial selected value for uncontrolled usage. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (value: string) => void - Fires when the selected value changes. |
| `onFocus` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void - Fires when a radio receives focus. |
| `onBlur` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void - Fires when a radio loses focus. |
| `label` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Text label for the group. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Helper text for the group. |
| `name` | string | — | Field name for form submission. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Required field indicator. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables all radio buttons in the group. |
| `error` | boolean | `false` | Displays the group in an error state. |
| `errorMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Error message displayed below the group. |
| `success` | boolean | `false` | Displays the group in a success state. |
| `successMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Success message displayed below the group. |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Loading state. |
| `size` | `"xs"` \| `"sm"` \| `"md"` \| `"lg"` \| `"xl"` \| number | `"md"` | Size of all radio indicators. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal"` \| `"vertical"` | `"vertical"` | Layout orientation. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for group sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Removes all default styling. |
| `reduceMotion` | `true` \| `false` \| `"auto"` | `"auto"` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects the user's OS setting. |
| `children` **(required)** | object | — | React.ReactNode - RadioButton children. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional class names applied to the group root. |

#### RadioButton

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` **(required)** | string | — | Unique value for this radio option. |
| `label` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Text label rendered beside the radio. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Helper text rendered below the label. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables this radio option. |
| `size` | `"xs"` \| `"sm"` \| `"md"` \| `"lg"` \| `"xl"` \| number | — | Size of the radio indicator. Inherits the group's size when unset. |
| `checkedIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Custom icon for the checked state. |
| `uncheckedIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode - Custom icon for the unchecked state. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for radio sub-elements. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional class names applied to the radio root. |

### Class overrides (RadioButton item)

```tsx
// `control` carries the base AND 2 state variants. Overriding it
// replaces all of them, so write them together:
<RadioButton
  classes={{
    control:
      "rounded-full border w-4 h-4 " +      // base
      "data-[state=checked]:bg-cl-accent data-[state=checked]:border-cl-accent " +
      "data-[state=unchecked]:bg-transparent ",
  }}
/>

// Passing only `control: "data-[state=checked]:…"` drops the base and the other 1 states.
```

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

Each is written or absent, never `"false"`.

**RadioGroup root** (`role="radiogroup"`):
- `data-disabled` — when `disabled`
- `data-loading` — when `loading`; the group disables its radios, which dim, and a spinner shows after the last one
- `data-reduce-motion` on that spinner, too, while reduced motion is in force
- `data-error` — when `error`
- `data-valid` — when `success` and not `error`
- `data-orientation="vertical" | "horizontal"` — from `orientation`
- `data-reduce-motion` — while reduced motion is in force

**RadioButton root** (the `<label>`):
- `data-state="checked" | "unchecked"` — always present
- `data-checked` — only while checked, for a selector that wants presence
- `data-disabled` — when the radio or its group is disabled or loading; it dims
- `data-loading` — when its group is loading; it dims as a disabled radio does
- `data-value` — the radio's `value`

**Control** (the circle): `data-state`, `data-checked`, `data-disabled` as on the root, and `data-error` / `data-valid` from the group. The checked control fills with the accent.

**Group message:** `data-invalid` on the error message, `data-valid` on the success message.

### Forms

- **Submitted value.** With `name`, it submits the checked radio's `value` under the group's `name`, and nothing when none is checked — the radios are native.
- **Reset.** A form reset — a `type="reset"` button or `form.reset()` — restores an uncontrolled group to `defaultValue` (or no selection), and the submitted value with it. Like a native input it fires no change callback: `onValueChange` is not called. A controlled RadioGroup is left alone: it keeps the `value` you pass and calls nothing, as a controlled React `<input>` does. Reset your own state in the form's `onReset` if you want the field cleared.
- **Required.** A `required` RadioGroup puts `required` on its radios: with none checked, it blocks the form's submit and the browser focuses the first radio. The field shows an error state only when you pass `error` and `errorMessage`.

### Keyboard Interactions

Native `<input type="radio">` elements in a group, so the browser owns the roving focus.

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves into the group, landing on the checked radio — or the first one when none is checked. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowRight` | Moves to the next radio and selects it. `ArrowUp`/`ArrowLeft` move back. |
| `Space` | Selects the focused radio. |

---

### Ref API

`RadioButton`'s ref lands on its `<input type="radio">`, as Checkbox's does, so `ref.current.focus()` focuses the radio and a form library can register it. `className` and the other HTML attributes still go on the `<label>`. `RadioGroup`'s ref is the group's root `<div>`.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
<RadioButton ref={ref} value="a" label="Apple" />
// ref.current is the <input type="radio">
```

---

## ResizablePanel

> A draggable resizable panel with constraints, keyboard resizing, Escape to cancel, and WAI-ARIA separator semantics.

**Category:** Layout
**Keywords:** resizable, panel, resize, drag, split, separator, divider, layout

### Import

```tsx
import { ResizablePanel } from "@chumlab/ui/resizable-panel";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { ResizablePanel } from "@chumlab/ui/resizable-panel";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanel defaultValue={300} minValue={150} maxValue={500}>
      <div style={{ padding: 16 }}>Drag the edge to resize.</div>
    </ResizablePanel>
  );
}
```

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

**Root (the panel):**
- `data-resizing` — while a pointer drag is resizing it
- `data-disabled` — when `disabled`
- `data-reduce-motion` — while reduced motion is in force

**Handle (`role="separator"`):**
- `data-resizing` — while a pointer drag is resizing the panel; the handle shows an accent bar for the length of the drag, the only time it paints anything by default
- `data-disabled` — when `disabled`; the handle is hidden and leaves the tab order
- `data-direction="left" | "right" | "top" | "bottom"` — the edge it sits on, from `resizeDirection`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from ResizablePanel.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | — | Controlled size value of the panel in pixels. |
| `defaultValue` | number | `300` | Default uncontrolled size value of the panel in pixels. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (value: number) => void — Callback fired when the panel size changes. |
| `onResizeStart` | object | — | (value: number) => void — Callback fired when a resize drag begins. |
| `onResizeEnd` | object | — | (value: number) => void — Callback fired when a resize drag ends. |
| `minValue` | number | `200` | Minimum allowed size value in pixels. |
| `maxValue` | number | `800` | Maximum allowed size value in pixels. |
| `resizeDirection` | `"left"` \| `"right"` \| `"top"` \| `"bottom"` | `"right"` | Direction from which the panel can be resized. |
| `step` | number | `10` | Step increment for resize value changes. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Whether the resize handle is disabled. |
| `reduceMotion` | boolean \| `"auto"` | `"auto"` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects the user's OS setting. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for sub-elements. |
| `handleContent` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom content rendered inside the resize handle. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | When true, removes all default styling. |

### Keyboard Interactions

The handle is `role="separator"` and focusable, so resizing never requires a drag (SC 2.5.7).

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the handle. |
| `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` | Resizes in steps. A vertical panel uses `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`. |
| `Home`, `End` | Jumps to the minimum or maximum size. |
| `Escape` | Abandons the resize and restores the size it started at. |

---

### Ref API

The ref lands on the handle, the `role="separator"` element a keyboard user tabs to and resizes with the arrow keys, so `ref.current.focus()` focuses it. `className`, `style` and the other HTML attributes still go on the panel itself.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
<ResizablePanel ref={ref} aria-label="Resize sidebar">…</ResizablePanel>
// ref.current is the separator
```

---

## SearchableDropdown

> A single-select dropdown with built-in search input, async search/prefetch, portal rendering, keyboard navigation, and full style customization.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** searchable, dropdown, select, combobox, search, filter, autocomplete, typeahead, async, listbox, form control

### Import

```tsx
import { SearchableDropdown } from "@chumlab/ui/searchable-dropdown";
import type { SearchableDropdownOption } from "@chumlab/ui/searchable-dropdown";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { SearchableDropdown } from "@chumlab/ui/searchable-dropdown";

const options = [
  { value: "apple", label: "Apple" },
  { value: "banana", label: "Banana" },
  { value: "cherry", label: "Cherry" },
];

export default function Example() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null);
  return (
    <SearchableDropdown
      options={options}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={(v) => setValue(v)}
      placeholder="Search fruits..."
    />
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `value` + `defaultValue` | Never combine. Use one or the other. |
| `value` requires `onValueChange` | Controlled mode — both needed together. |
| `open` requires `onOpenChange` | Controlled open state — both needed together. |
| `searchOptions` | Async search function. Replaces local filtering when provided. |
| `loadInitialOptions` | Requires `loadInitialOnOpen={true}` to trigger on open. |
| `searchDebounce` | Only applies to `searchOptions`. Default: `300`. |
| `showSearch` | Default `true`. Set `false` to hide search input. |
| `clearable` | Only works when a value is selected. |
| `forceDropdownSide` | Only meaningful with `dropdownSide`. Disables auto-flip. |
| `lockScroll` | Prevents body scroll while open. Default: `false`. |
| `renderTrigger` | `renderTrigger(triggerProps, state)` replaces the default `<button>`. Spread `triggerProps` onto a `<button>`: it is exactly what the default trigger renders, ref and `type="button"` included. Draw from `state` (`isOpen`, `selectedOption`, `placeholder`), which never reaches the DOM. |
| `name` | Renders a hidden `<input>` for native form submission. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

**Root element:**
- `data-disabled` — when `disabled={true}`
- `data-error` — when `error={true}`
- `data-open` — when dropdown is open
- `data-full-width` — when `fullWidth={true}`
- `data-valid` — when `success={true}`

**Trigger element:**
- `data-disabled`, `data-error`, `data-open` — mirrors root
- `data-placeholder` — when no option is selected; the placeholder text is tertiary

**Dropdown panel:**
- `data-position` — `"top"` or `"bottom"` (actual rendered position)
- `data-state="open" | "closed"`
- `data-dropdown-id` — unique ID for click-outside detection
- `data-side` — on the surface, the side it was placed on after any flip

**Options:**
- `data-selected` — a selected option; it shows the selected icon
- `data-highlighted` — the keyboard position
- `data-disabled` — a disabled option
- `data-value` — the option's value

**Messages:** `data-invalid` on the error message

DOM nesting: `root > label + description + wrapper > trigger(combobox) + content(portal) > searchInput + optionList(listbox) > options`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from SearchableDropdown.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `options` | array | `[]` | Array of dropdown options. Mutually exclusive with `searchOptions`: the async branch never reads it. |
| `value` | string \| null | — | Controlled selected value. |
| `defaultValue` | string | — | Default uncontrolled selected value. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (value: string \| null, option: SearchableDropdownOption \| null) => void — Callback fired when the selected value changes. |
| `open` | boolean | — | Controlled open state of the dropdown. |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Default uncontrolled open state. |
| `onOpenChange` | object | — | (open: boolean) => void — Callback fired when the open state changes. |
| `id` | string | — | HTML id attribute for the component. |
| `name` | string | — | Form field name attribute. |
| `placeholder` | object | `"Select an option"` | React.ReactNode — Placeholder content shown when no value is selected. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Whether the dropdown is disabled. |
| `error` | boolean | `false` | Whether the dropdown is in an error state. |
| `errorMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Error message displayed below the dropdown. |
| `label` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Label displayed above the dropdown. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Description text displayed below the label. |
| `success` | boolean | `false` | Whether the dropdown is in a success state. |
| `successMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Success message displayed below the dropdown. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Whether the field is required. |
| `clearable` | boolean | `false` | Whether the selected value can be cleared. |
| `showSearch` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show the search input in the dropdown. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | string | `"Search..."` | Placeholder text for the search input. |
| `searchInputAriaLabel` | string | `"Search options"` | Custom aria-label for the search input. Defaults to 'Search options'. |
| `emptyContent` | object | `"No results found"` | React.ReactNode — Content shown when no search results are found. |
| `showChevron` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show the chevron icon on the trigger. |
| `showSelectedIcon` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show a check icon on the selected option. |
| `selectedIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom icon for the selected option. |
| `fullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Whether the dropdown expands to fill its parent container. |
| `loading` | boolean | — | Whether the dropdown is in a loading state. |
| `searchOptions` | object | — | (query: string) => Promise<SearchableDropdownOption[]> — Async search callback for server-side filtering. Mutually exclusive with `options`. |
| `searchDebounce` | number | `300` | Debounce delay in milliseconds for the search callback. |
| `initialOptions` | array | `[]` | Initial options to display before any search is performed. Async branch only (`searchOptions`). |
| `loadInitialOptions` | object | — | () => Promise<SearchableDropdownOption[]> — Async callback to load initial options. Async branch only, and requires `loadInitialOnOpen`. |
| `loadInitialOnOpen` | boolean | `false` | Whether to load initial options when the dropdown opens. Requires `loadInitialOptions`; alone it has nothing to load. |
| `onLoadError` | object | — | (error: unknown) => void — Callback when async loading fails. |
| `shimmerCount` | number | `5` | Number of shimmer placeholder items to show while loading. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for sub-elements. |
| `className` | string | — | CSS class for the root element. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles applied to the root element. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Whether to keep the dropdown DOM mounted when closed. |
| `portalContainer` | object | — | HTMLElement \| null — Custom container element for the dropdown portal. |
| `dropdownSide` | `"top"` \| `"bottom"` | `"bottom"` | Position of the dropdown relative to the trigger. |
| `forceDropdownSide` | boolean | `false` | When true, locks the dropdown to the specified dropdownSide without auto-flipping. |
| `dropdownZIndex` | number | `50` | Z-index for the dropdown. |
