### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** — uses `DEFAULT_TABLE_CLASSES`
2. **Partial override** — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.
3. **Unstyled** — all slots empty, you build from scratch

#### Key slots

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Root container | `root` |
| Table element | `list` |
| Header row/cell | `header`, `headerCell` |
| Body row/cell | `item`, `cell` |
| Selected row | `selectedRow` |
| Pinned columns | `pinnedRegion`, `pinnedList` |
| Scrollable area | `scrollRegion` (has `overflow-x-auto`) |
| Empty state | `empty` |
| Shimmer loading | `loading`, `loadingRow`, `loadingItem`, `loadingBar` |
| Search bar | `searchInput`, `searchInput` |

#### Responsive behavior

The table uses a flex layout with `overflow-x-auto` on the unpinned container, allowing horizontal scroll on mobile. Cell content uses `whitespace-nowrap` by default.

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix. When overriding, always provide both variants.

---

### Patterns

#### With pagination

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
const [rows, setRows] = useState(10);
const paginatedData = data.slice((page - 1) * rows, page * rows);
<Table columns={columns} data={paginatedData} />
<Pagination value={page} totalPages={Math.ceil(data.length / rows)} onValueChange={setPage} />
```

#### Sortable with controlled state

```tsx
const [sorting, setSorting] = useState<SortingState>([]);
<Table columns={columns} data={data} sortable sorting={sorting} onSortingChange={setSorting} />
```

#### Row selection

```tsx
<Table columns={columns} data={data} selectionMode="multiple" onSelectedRowIdsChange={(rows) => console.log(rows)} />
```

#### Column pinning

```tsx
const [pinned, setPinned] = useState<string[]>(["name"]);

<Table columns={columns} data={data} pinnableColumns={["name", "email"]} pinnedColumns={pinned} onPinnedColumnsChange={setPinned} />
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

Cell navigation is on the grid itself; the controls inside a cell keep their own behaviour.

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves between the interactive elements — search, filter triggers, resize handles, the controls in a cell. |
| `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` | Moves the focused cell along a row. `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` move down a column. |
| `Home`, `End` | Moves to the first or last cell in the row. |
| `Ctrl+Home`, `Ctrl+End` | Moves to the first cell in the first row, or the last cell in the last row. The header row is not part of this navigation: its sort, filter and pin buttons are reached with `Tab`. |
| `Enter` | Opens the focused control: a filter dialog, or an editable cell when `editable` is set. In the editor, commits the edit and returns focus to the cell. |
| `F2` | Opens the focused cell's editor when `editable` is set. |
| `Escape` | Closes the filter dialog and returns focus to its trigger, or abandons an edit in progress and returns focus to the cell. Always: there is no prop to turn it off, because the APG dialog pattern requires Escape to close the filter dialog. |
| `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` on a resize handle | Resizes the column in steps, so column widths are reachable without a drag (SC 2.5.7). |

---

---

## TabPanel

> Accessible tab panel with icons, badges, tooltips, vertical orientation, keep-mounted panels, and roving tabindex.

**Category:** Navigation
**Keywords:** tabs, tab panel, tabbed interface, navigation tabs, tab list, tab content, vertical tabs, keep mounted

### Import

```tsx
import { TabPanel } from "@chumlab/ui/tab-panel";
import type { Tab, TabPanelProps } from "@chumlab/ui/tab-panel";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { TabPanel } from "@chumlab/ui/tab-panel";

const tabs = [
  { id: "home", label: "Home" },
  { id: "profile", label: "Profile" },
  { id: "settings", label: "Settings" },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <TabPanel tabs={tabs} defaultValue="home">
      {(item) => <div style={{ padding: 16 }}>{item.label} content</div>}
    </TabPanel>
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `tabs` | **Required.** Array of `Tab` objects with unique `id`. |
| `value` + `onValueChange` | Controlled mode — both needed together. |
| `defaultValue` | Uncontrolled mode — do not combine with `value`. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal"` (default) or `"vertical"`. |
| `activationMode` | `"automatic"` (default) or `"manual"` (Enter/Space to activate). |
| `children` | Render function `(tab) => ReactNode`. This is how panel content is rendered — not a `renderContent` prop or `content` on tab objects. |
| `renderTab` | Custom tab renderer. Receives `(props, defaultElement)`. |
| `keepMounted` | `false` (default) mounts only the active panel, `"visited"` keeps every panel opened so far, `true` mounts every panel including ones never opened. |
| `unstyled` | Strips all defaults. Must provide styling via `classes`. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

- `data-state="active"` / `data-state="inactive"` — on tab buttons
- `data-disabled` — on disabled tabs
- `data-orientation` — on tablist and root
- `data-reduce-motion="true"` — on the root, while reduced motion is in force
- `data-state` is also on the label, the icon and the count badge inside each
  tab, not only on the button — which is what makes
  `classes={{ count: "data-[state=active]:bg-cl-accent/10" }}` work

DOM nesting: `root > list(role="tablist") > item(role="tab") + indicator > content(role="tabpanel")`

#### Slot → element

| Slot | Element |
|------|---------|
| `root` | The outer container. |
| `list` | The tablist strip holding every tab button. |
| `item` | One tab button. Carries `data-state` and `data-disabled`. |
| `itemText` | The tab's label text, so it can be hidden at narrow widths without hiding the icon. |
| `itemIcon` | The icon inside a tab. |
| `count` | The count badge. Ships with shape only — no fill — so a filled badge is a `classes` override. |
| `indicator` | The active-tab indicator. |
| `content` | The panel below the strip. |

There is no `tabList`, `tab`, `tabActive`, `tabInactive`, `tabFocus`,
`tabDisabled`, `iconActive`, `iconInactive`, `countActive`, `countInactive` or
`panel` slot. State is a variant on a slot, not a slot of its own.

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from TabPanel.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `tabs` **(required)** | array | — | Array of tab definitions. |
| `id` | string | — | HTML id attribute. |
| `value` | string | — | Controlled active tab ID. |
| `defaultValue` | string | — | Default uncontrolled active tab ID. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (tabId: string) => void — Callback fired when the active tab changes. |
| `children` | object | — | React.ReactNode \| ((tab: Tab) => ReactNode) — Tab panel content, either static or a render function. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal"` \| `"vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Layout orientation of the tab list. |
| `activationMode` | `"automatic"` \| `"manual"` | `"automatic"` | Whether tabs activate automatically on focus or require manual activation. |
| `loop` | boolean | `true` | Whether keyboard navigation loops from last tab to first. |
| `iconPosition` | `"start"` \| `"end"` | `"start"` | Which end of the tab label its icon sits at: `start` before the text, `end` after it. |
| `showZeroCount` | boolean | `false` | Whether to show a count badge when the count is zero. |
| `alwaysShowLabels` | boolean | `true` | Whether to always show tab labels (even when icons are present). |
| `showTooltips` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show tooltips on tabs. |
| `tooltipSide` | `"top"` \| `"bottom"` \| `"left"` \| `"right"` | `"bottom"` | Position of tab tooltips. |
| `tooltipOffset` | number | `4` | Offset distance for tab tooltips in pixels. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Whether the entire tab panel is disabled. |
| `reduceMotion` | boolean \| `"auto"` | `"auto"` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects the user's OS setting. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | When true, removes all default styling. |
| `renderTab` | object | — | (props: TabRenderProps, defaultElement: React.ReactElement) => ReactNode — Custom tab render function. |
| `aria-label` | string | — | Accessible label for the tab list. |
| `aria-labelledby` | string | — | ID of the element that labels the tab list. |
| `aria-describedby` | string | — | Ids of the elements that describe the tab list. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for sub-elements. |
| `className` | string | — | CSS class for the root element. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles applied to the root element. |
| `keepMounted` | `false` \| `"visited"` \| `true` | `false` | Which panels' content is in the DOM: `false` the active panel only, `"visited"` every panel opened so far, `true` every panel, including ones never opened. |

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** — uses `DEFAULT_TABPANEL_CLASSES`
2. **Partial override** — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** — all slots empty, you build from scratch

```tsx
// `item` carries the base AND 3 state variants. Overriding it
// replaces all of them, so write them together:
<TabPanel
  classes={{
    item:
      "rounded-cl-md px-2 py-1 " +           // base
      "data-[disabled]:opacity-50 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed " +
      "data-[state=active]:text-cl-accent " +
      "data-[state=inactive]:text-cl-text-tertiary ",
  }}
/>

// Passing only `item: "data-[disabled]:…"` drops the base and the other
// 2 states.
```

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root (w-full)
├── list (role="tablist", flex overflow-x-auto)
│   └── item (role="item", relative shrink-0)
│       ├── itemIcon
│       ├── itemText
│       ├── count (badge)
│       └── indicator (absolute bottom, animated underline)
└── content (role="tabpanel", p-4)
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Tab list container | `list` |
| Tab button | `item` |
| Tab focus ring | `tabFocus` |
| Tab label text | `itemText` |
| Tab icon | `itemIcon` |
| Count badge | `count` |
| Active underline | `indicator` |
| Panel content | `content` |

#### Responsive sizing

Default tab list uses `overflow-x-auto` with `gap-4 sm:gap-6`. Tabs use `shrink-0` + `text-xs sm:text-sm` + `py-2.5 sm:py-3` for compact mobile sizing.

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix. When overriding, always provide both variants.

---

### Patterns

#### Controlled tabs

```tsx
const [active, setActive] = useState("home");
<TabPanel tabs={tabs} value={active} onValueChange={setActive}>{(item) => ...}</TabPanel>
```

#### With icons and badges

```tsx
const tabs = [
  { id: "home", itemText: "Home", itemIcon: HomeIcon, count: 3 },
  { id: "messages", itemText: "Messages", itemIcon: MailIcon, count: 12 },
];
```

#### Keep panels mounted

`keepMounted` takes three values: `false` (default) mounts only the active panel, `"visited"` keeps every panel opened so far, and `true` mounts every panel, including ones never opened.

```tsx
<TabPanel tabs={tabs} keepMounted="visited">{(item) => <Panel id={item.id} />}</TabPanel>
```

#### Vertical orientation

```tsx
<TabPanel tabs={tabs} orientation="vertical" />
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves into the tab list, landing on the active tab, then out to the panel. |
| `ArrowRight`, `ArrowLeft` | Moves between tabs; a vertical list uses `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp`, and right-to-left swaps the horizontal pair. With `activationMode="automatic"` the tab activates as focus lands. |
| `Home`, `End` | Moves to the first or last tab. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Activates the focused tab under `activationMode="manual"`. |

---

---

## TextArea

> A production-grade multi-line text input with auto-resize, character count, validation states, icons, and full form integration.

**Category:** Form
**Keywords:** textarea, text area, multiline input, form, auto resize, character count, validation

### Import

```tsx
import { TextArea, TextAreaLabel } from "@chumlab/ui/textarea";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { TextArea } from "@chumlab/ui/textarea";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", gap: 16, maxWidth: 480 }}>
      <TextArea label="Message" placeholder="Write your message..." />
      <TextArea
        label="Bio"
        placeholder="Tell us about yourself..."
        description="Max 200 characters"
        maxLength={200}
        showCount
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `showCount` | Requires `maxLength` to be set |
| `autoResize` | Overrides manual `resize` CSS. Sets `overflow: hidden` and `resize: none`. |
| `size` | Sets the control's padding and type: 28/40/52px fields, 30/42/54 with the border. Emits `data-size` as well, for CSS that wants it |
| `onStartIconClick` | Requires `startIconAriaLabel` for accessibility |
| `onEndIconClick` | Requires `endIconAriaLabel` for accessibility |

---

### Data Attributes

- `data-size` on root — "sm", "md", "lg"
- `data-disabled` on root — when disabled
- `data-error` on root — when error state
- `data-valid` on root — when success state
- `data-readonly` on root — when readOnly
- `data-loading` on root — when loading: the field dims, takes no input, and shows a spinner
- `data-reduce-motion` on that spinner — while reduced motion is in force
- `data-invalid` on the error message
- `data-slot="textarea"` on the textarea element
- `data-slot="count"` on the character count

DOM nesting: `root > label + description + wrapper(startIcon + textarea + endIcon + clear + loader) + error/success + count`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from TextArea.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Label displayed above the textarea. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Description text below the label. |
| `error` | boolean | `false` | Whether the textarea is in an error state. |
| `errorMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Error message displayed below the textarea. |
| `success` | boolean | `false` | Green success state for validated fields. |
| `successMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Success message displayed below the textarea. |
| `size` | `"sm"` \| `"md"` \| `"lg"` | — | Sets the control's padding and type size together: a 28, 40 and 52px field, 30/42/54 with its border. Also emits data-size on the root for CSS to target; the attribute is a hook beside the sizing, not the sizing itself. |
| `startIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Icon rendered before the textarea. |
| `endIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Icon rendered after the textarea. |
| `onStartIconClick` | object | — | (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void — Makes startIcon a clickable button, called with the native click event. |
| `onEndIconClick` | object | — | (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void — Makes endIcon a clickable button, called with the native click event. |
| `startIconAriaLabel` | string | — | Accessible label for startIcon when clickable. Required with onStartIconClick. |
| `endIconAriaLabel` | string | — | Accessible label for endIcon when clickable. Required with onEndIconClick. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (value: string) => void — Fires with the current string value when the value changes. |
| `clearable` | boolean | `false` | Show a built-in clear button when the textarea has a value. |
| `onClear` | object | — | () => void — Callback when the clear button is clicked. |
| `showCount` | boolean | `false` | Show character count (requires maxLength to be set). |
| `autoResize` | boolean | `false` | Automatically resize height to fit content. |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Whether the textarea is in a loading state. |
| `loader` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom loader element. |
| `loaderSize` | number | `16` | Size of the default CircularLoader in pixels. |
| `fullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Whether the textarea expands to fill its parent container. |
| `className` | string | — | CSS class for the root container element. |
| `classes` | object | — | Slot-based class overrides for internal elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | When true, all default classes are removed; only classes overrides apply. |
| `placeholder` | string | — | Placeholder text for the textarea. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Whether the textarea is disabled. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Whether the field is required. |
| `name` | string | — | Form field name attribute. |
| `id` | string | — | HTML id attribute. |
| `rows` | number | `4` | Number of visible text rows. |
| `maxLength` | number | — | Maximum number of characters allowed. |
| `value` | string | — | Controlled value of the textarea. |
| `defaultValue` | string | — | Default uncontrolled value. |

### Sub-component Props

Generated from the types by `scripts/build-subcomponent-schemas.mjs`.

#### TextAreaLabel

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | The label's content. |
| `required` | `boolean \| undefined` | Marks the field required and draws the required indicator. |
| `htmlFor` | `string \| undefined` | The id of the control this labels. Set automatically when the label is rendered by the field. |
| `className` | `string \| undefined` | Additional classes for the root element. |

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

A restyle that drops the box, such as an underline, must also replace the focus ring: pass `focus-within:ring-0` and mark focus on the edge you keep, or the default `focus-within:ring-2` survives the merge and the field focuses as a box.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** — uses `DEFAULT_TEXTAREA_CLASSES` with dark mode, focus ring
2. **Partial override** — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** — all slots empty

#### Slot → visual mapping

```
root (flex flex-col)
├── label
├── description
├── control (border, focus ring)
│   ├── startIcon
│   ├── input
│   ├── endIcon
│   ├── clear button
│   └── loader
├── message / message
└── count
```

| "I want to change..." | Slot | Notes |
|------------------------|------|-------|
| Border/focus ring | `control` | Contains textarea chrome |
| Textarea text | `input` | Font, color, placeholder, resize |
| Label style | `label` | Font weight, size, color |
| Error text | `message` | Color, icon |
| The whole field and its labelling | `root` | The outer wrapper; `fullWidth` adds `w-full` here |
| The character counter | `count` | Shown under the field when `showCount` is set |

#### Dark mode

Defaults include `dark:` variants. When overriding, provide both light and dark.

---

### Patterns

#### Auto-resize textarea

```tsx
<TextArea autoResize rows={2} label="Notes" placeholder="Start typing..." />
```

#### With character count

```tsx
<TextArea label="Bio" showCount maxLength={500} placeholder="Tell us about yourself..." />
```

#### With validation

```tsx
<TextArea
  label="Feedback"
  error={!isValid}
  errorMessage="Feedback is required"
  success={isValid}
  successMessage="Thank you!"
  required
/>
```

---

### Forms

- **Submitted value.** With `name`, it submits the text, from the native textarea.
- **Reset.** A form reset — a `type="reset"` button or `form.reset()` — restores an uncontrolled textarea to `defaultValue` (or empty), and the submitted value with it. Like a native input it fires no change callback: `onValueChange` is not called. A controlled TextArea is left alone: it keeps the `value` you pass and calls nothing, as a controlled React `<input>` does. Reset your own state in the form's `onReset` if you want the field cleared.
- **Required.** An empty `required` TextArea blocks the form's submit and the browser focuses it. The field shows an error state only when you pass `error` and `errorMessage`.

### Keyboard Interactions

A native `<textarea>`: the browser owns text entry and selection.

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the field, and out of it — it does not insert a tab character. |

---

---

## TimePicker

> A time input with dropdown list or analog clock variant, smart parsing, 12/24-hour formats, min/max constraints, clearable, keyboard navigation, and full accessibility.

**Category:** form
**Keywords:** time picker, time input, clock, dropdown, 12h, 24h, AM PM, time selection, clock face, time format

### Import

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from "@chumlab/ui/time-picker";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from "@chumlab/ui/time-picker";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function Example() {
  const [time, setTime] = useState<string | null>(null);
  return <TimePicker value={time} onValueChange={(t) => setTime(t)} />;
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints (critical for correct usage)

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `mode` | `"dropdown"` (default) shows a list; `"clock"` shows an analog clock face. |
| `format` | `"24h"` (default) or `"12h"`. Affects display, parsing, and option generation. |
| `minuteStep` | Clamped to 1-60. Invalid values (0, NaN, negatives) are auto-corrected. |
| `minTime` / `maxTime` | Format: `"HH:MM"`. Dims/disables out-of-range options in both variants, and a typed time outside them is not committed: the field shows its error state with `aria-invalid`. |
| `keepMounted` | Only affects dropdown variant. Clock always remounts to reset selection mode. |
| `open` + `onOpenChange` | For controlled open state. Don't mix with `defaultOpen`. |
| `value` + `onValueChange` | For controlled mode. Don't mix with `defaultValue`. |
| `forceDropdownSide` | When true, locks to `dropdownSide` without auto-flipping. |
| `lockScroll` | Prevents body scroll when dropdown/clock is open. |
| `fullWidth` | Applies `width: 100%` to root and trigger, overriding class widths. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

- `data-disabled` — on root and trigger when `disabled`
- `data-error` — on root and trigger when `error`, or when the typed time is outside `minTime`/`maxTime`
- `data-valid` — on root and trigger when `success` and not `error`
- `data-open` — on root and trigger when dropdown/clock is open
- `data-loading` — on root, and on the control holding the trigger, when `loading`; the control dims and takes no pointer input
- `data-selected` — on selected option
- `data-highlighted` — on keyboard-focused option
- `data-position` — on dropdown portal (`"top"` or `"bottom"`)
- `data-side` — on the dropdown's surface, the side it was placed on after any flip
- `data-active` — on active clock display button and period button; `data-state="active"` on the same buttons
- `data-inner` — on a clock number in the inner (13–24) ring of the 24-hour face
- `data-invalid` on the error message, `data-valid` on the success message

DOM nesting: `root > label + description + wrapper(trigger(input + clear + chevron) + portal(dropdown|clock)) + error/success`

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from TimePicker.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | string \| null | — | Current time value (e.g. '14:30' or '2:30 PM'). |
| `defaultValue` | string \| null | — | Default time value for uncontrolled usage. |
| `onValueChange` | object | — | (time: string \| null, timeValue: TimeValue \| null) => void — Called when the selected time changes. |
| `onBlur` | object | — | (event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void — Fires once focus has left the whole time picker, with the input's native blur event. |
| `format` | `"12h"` \| `"24h"` | `"24h"` | Time display format. |
| `minuteStep` | number | `15` | Minute interval for dropdown options and clock snapping. Clamped to 1-60. |
| `minTime` | string | — | Minimum selectable time (e.g. '09:00'). A typed time before it is not committed, and the field shows its error state with aria-invalid. |
| `maxTime` | string | — | Maximum selectable time (e.g. '17:00'). A typed time after it is not committed, and the field shows its error state with aria-invalid. |
| `name` | string | — | Name for the hidden input for form submission. |
| `placeholder` | string | — | Placeholder text for the input. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables the component. |
| `error` | boolean | `false` | Marks the component as having an error. |
| `errorMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Error message displayed below the input. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Helper text displayed below the label. |
| `success` | boolean | — | Success state. |
| `successMessage` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Success message text. |
| `loading` | boolean | — | Loading state. |
| `label` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Label displayed above the input. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Shows a required indicator on the label. |
| `showEndIcon` | boolean | `true` | Show the chevron/end icon in the trigger. |
| `endIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom end icon element replacing the default chevron. |
| `showSelectedIcon` | boolean | `true` | Show a check icon on the selected option. |
| `selectedIcon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom selected icon element. |
| `renderOptionContent` | object | — | (time: string, isSelected: boolean) => ReactNode — Custom renderer for dropdown option content. |
| `fullWidth` | boolean | `false` | Expand the picker to fill its parent container. |
| `mode` | `"dropdown"` \| `"clock"` | `"dropdown"` | How a time is picked: a dropdown list or an analog clock face. |
| `clearable` | boolean | `true` | Show a clear button when a value is selected. |
| `onClear` | object | — | () => void — Called when the clear button is clicked. |
| `open` | boolean | — | Controlled open state. |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Default open state (uncontrolled). |
| `onOpenChange` | object | — | (open: boolean) => void — Called when the open state changes. |
| `lockScroll` | boolean | `false` | Lock body scroll when dropdown is open. |
| `dropdownSide` | `"top"` \| `"bottom"` | `"bottom"` | Position of the dropdown relative to the trigger. |
| `forceDropdownSide` | boolean | `false` | When true, locks the dropdown to the specified position without auto-flipping. |
| `dropdownZIndex` | number | `50` | Z-index for the dropdown. |
| `dropdownOffset` | number | `4` | Gap between trigger and dropdown in pixels. |
| `keepMounted` | boolean | `false` | Keep dropdown DOM mounted when closed (dropdown mode only). |
| `portalContainer` | object | — | HTMLElement \| null — Custom container element for the dropdown portal. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for all sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | Omits built-in layout helpers so layout comes entirely from classes. |
| `reduceMotion` | boolean \| `"auto"` | `false` | Controls motion preferences. 'auto' respects the user's OS prefers-reduced-motion setting. |
| `onCancel` | object | — | () => void — Called when the clock cancel button is pressed. |
| `onConfirm` | object | — | () => void — Called when the clock confirm button is pressed. |
| `cancelText` | string | `"Cancel"` | Text for the clock cancel button. |
| `confirmText` | string | `"OK"` | Text for the clock OK button. |

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### How class merging works

1. **Default** (no `classes`, no `unstyled`) — uses `DEFAULT_TIMEPICKER_CLASSES`
2. **Partial override** (`classes` without `unstyled`) — your classes compose with that slot's defaults; slots you don't name keep theirs.

**A plain utility of yours wins over every default in its group on that slot, states included.**
`classes={{ control: "bg-green-500" }}` paints green in every state, where a default
`data-[state=checked]:` background would otherwise keep winning. To restyle one state only,
pass that state's own variant (`data-[state=checked]:bg-green-500`). Defaults in other groups stay.

3. **Unstyled** (`unstyled={true}`) — all slots empty, you provide everything

```tsx
// `clockNumber` carries the base AND 2 state variants. Overriding it
// replaces all of them, so write them together:
<TimePicker
  classes={{
    clockNumber:
      "rounded-cl-md px-2 py-1 " +           // base
      "data-[disabled]:opacity-50 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed " +
      "data-[selected]:bg-cl-accent/15 data-[selected]:text-cl-accent ",
  }}
/>

// Passing only `clockNumber: "data-[disabled]:…"` drops the base and the other
// 1 states.
```

#### Key slots

| "I want to change..." | Slot to use |
|------------------------|-------------|
| Root container | `root` |
| Label text | `label` |
| Trigger button area | `trigger` |
| Text input | `input` |
| Chevron icon | `icon` |
| Clear button | `clearTrigger` |
| Dropdown panel | `content` |
| Option list container | `list` |
| Individual option | `item` |
| Selected option highlight | `optionSelected` |
| Focused option highlight | `optionFocused` |
| Check icon in option | `itemIndicator` |
| Error message | `message` |
| Description text | `description` |
| Clock container | `clockContent` |
| Clock face circle | `clockFace` |
| Clock numbers | `clockNumber` |
| Clock hand | `clockHand`, `clockHandLine`, `clockHandDot` |
| AM/PM buttons | `periodTrigger` |
| OK/Cancel buttons | `confirmTrigger`, `cancelTrigger` |

#### Dark mode

Defaults use Tailwind `dark:` prefix, activated by `<html class="dark">`. When overriding a slot, always provide both light and dark variants.

#### Responsive behavior

Default trigger has `w-56` (224px). Use `fullWidth` prop or override `trigger` class with `w-full` for fluid layouts. Clock face is `w-52 h-52` by default.

---

### Patterns

#### Controlled state

```tsx
const [time, setTime] = useState<string | null>(null);
<TimePicker value={time} onValueChange={(t) => setTime(t)} />
```

#### 12-hour format with constraints

```tsx
<TimePicker format="12h" minTime="09:00" maxTime="17:00" minuteStep={30} />
```

#### Clock variant

```tsx
<TimePicker
  mode="clock"
  format="12h"
  onConfirm={() => console.log("confirmed")}
  onCancel={() => console.log("cancelled")}
/>
```

#### Force dropdown position

```tsx
<TimePicker dropdownSide="bottom" forceDropdownSide lockScroll />
```

#### Form submission

```tsx
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <TimePicker name="meetingTime" label="Meeting Time" required />
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
```

---

### Forms

- **Submitted value.** With `name`, it submits one entry, the time as the field holds it (`09:30`, or `2:30 PM` in 12-hour format), or an empty string when there is none.
- **Reset.** A form reset — a `type="reset"` button or `form.reset()` — restores an uncontrolled time to `defaultValue` (or no time), clearing any out-of-range error from a typed time, and the submitted value with it. Like a native input it fires no change callback: `onValueChange` is not called. A controlled TimePicker is left alone: it keeps the `value` you pass and calls nothing, as a controlled React `<input>` does. Reset your own state in the form's `onReset` if you want the field cleared.
- **Required.** An empty `required` TimePicker blocks the form's submit, and the browser's validation moves focus to the time input. The field shows an error state only when you pass `error` and `errorMessage`.
- **Disabled.** A disabled TimePicker submits nothing, as a disabled native control doesn't.

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| Typing | Sets the time: `hh:mm` on a 24-hour picker, `hh:mm am` or `hh:mm pm` on a 12-hour one, committed on `Enter`, `Tab` or leaving the field. Any minute can be typed, not only the `minuteStep` ones the list and the clock offer: the step is the increment offered, not a constraint. A time outside `minTime` and `maxTime` is not committed: the field keeps the text, shows its error state with `aria-invalid`, and `onValueChange` is not called. Typing opens the panel; `Space` is a character, the one between the time and AM/PM. |
| `Backspace` | Deleting the whole value and committing it clears the time. So does the clear button, which `Tab` reaches. |
| `Enter` | In the dropdown list, picks the highlighted time. Otherwise commits what was typed and closes the panel. |
| `Tab` | Commits what was typed, closes the panel and moves to the next control. |
| `Escape` | Closes the panel; focus stays in the input, which is where it was. Always: there is no prop to turn it off, because the APG combobox pattern requires Escape to close the popup. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | Opens the dropdown list and moves through its times. On the clock variant, `ArrowDown` opens the clock and neither key does anything else: there is no list to move through, so nothing is highlighted and `Enter` commits what was typed. |
| `Home`, `End` | Jumps to the first or last time in the dropdown list. On the clock variant they move the caret. |
| `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `PageUp`, `PageDown` | Move the caret in the input. The clock is a pointer affordance: focus stays in the input while it is open, its face takes no keyboard focus, and its own handling of the arrow keys, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Home` and `End` is not reachable from the keyboard. Every time the clock can set can be typed. |

---

### Ref API

The ref lands on the trigger, which for TimePicker is the typed text `<input role="combobox">` a keyboard user tabs to, so `ref.current.focus()` focuses the field — which is what a form library calls on the first invalid field.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
<TimePicker ref={ref} label="Time" />
// ref.current is the trigger <input>
```

---

## Toast

> A notification system for displaying brief messages. Supports multiple variants, positions, progress bars, custom content, and auto-dismiss.

**Category:** Feedback
**Keywords:** toast, notification, alert, snackbar, message, flash message, status

### Import

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from "@chumlab/ui/toast";
```

---

### Setup

Toast is the one component in the library with a structural requirement: it is
not something you place where you want it. `ToastProvider` wraps your tree once,
high enough that every caller is inside it, and toasts are created by calling a
function rather than rendering an element.

```tsx
// app root — once, around everything
import { ToastProvider } from "@chumlab/ui/toast";

export default function App({ children }) {
  return <ToastProvider position="top-right">{children}</ToastProvider>;
}
```

```tsx
// any child — no element, no state of your own
import { useToast } from "@chumlab/ui/toast";

function SaveButton() {
  const toast = useToast();
  return <button onClick={() => toast.success("Saved")}>Save</button>;
}
```

Three things that follow from that, and are the ones missed first:

- **`useToast()` throws outside the provider.** If you get that error, the
  component calling it is mounted above the wrap, or in a different React tree —
  a separate `createRoot`, or a portal rendered outside the provider's subtree.
- **One provider, not one per page.** Position, duration and `maxToasts` are the
  provider's props, so a second one gives you two independent stacks that do not
  know about each other's limits.
- **You never render `<Toast>` yourself.** It is exported for typing; the
  provider renders it, gives it its `id`, and removes it once your `onDismiss(id)` has run.

There is no Anatomy section for this, deliberately: the thing nested inside
`ToastProvider` is your tree, not another Toast part, and a diagram naming one
element would say less than the two snippets above.

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from "@chumlab/ui/toast";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <MyComponent />
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}

function MyComponent() {
  const toast = useToast();
  return (
    <button onClick={() => toast.success("Saved successfully!")}>
      Save
    </button>
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `variant` | `"success"`, `"warning"`, `"error"`, `"info"` |
| `position` | Set on `<ToastProvider>`. 6 options: `"bottom-right"` (default), `"top-right"`, `"top-left"`, `"top-center"`, `"bottom-left"`, `"bottom-center"` |
| `duration` | Milliseconds before auto-dismiss. `0` = persistent. Default `5000` for every type. |
| `classes.root` | Class string for the toast's outer element. It does not replace the layout. |
| `onDismiss` | Fires when the toast is dismissed, by timeout or the close button |
| `maxToasts` | Set on `<ToastProvider>` to limit visible toasts |

---

### API Methods

```tsx
const toast = useToast();
toast.success("title", options?);
toast.warning("title", options?);
toast.error("title", options?);
toast.info("title", options?);
toast.toast({ variant, message, ...options }); // generic
toast.dismiss(id);
toast.dismissAll();
```

---

### Keyboard Interactions

A toast takes focus only when it has an action; otherwise it announces itself and stays out of the tab order.

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Escape` | Dismisses the newest toast, and fires its `onDismiss`. An open Modal, Drawer, menu or tooltip takes the key first, and the toast is left alone. On by default; `closeOnEscape={false}` on the provider turns it off. |
| `Tab` | Moves to the toast's action and close button while it is on screen. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Activates the focused action. |

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from Toast.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` **(required)** | string | — | Unique identifier for the toast, rendered as its root's id. |
| `variant` | `"success"` \| `"warning"` \| `"error"` \| `"info"` | `"info"` | Which status this is, choosing the colour and the status glyph. |
| `message` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Primary message content. |
| `description` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Secondary description text. |
| `content` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom content that replaces message and description. |
| `duration` | number | `5000` | Auto-dismiss duration in milliseconds. |
| `showProgress` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show a progress bar countdown. |
| `progressColor` | string | — | Custom color for the progress bar. |
| `icon` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Custom icon replacing the variant's default icon. |
| `showCloseButton` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show a close/dismiss button. |
| `onDismiss` | object | — | (id: string) => void — Fires with the toast's `id` when it is dismissed: its close button, Escape, or its duration running out. |
| `role` | `"alert"` \| `"status"` | — | ARIA role for the toast element. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles applied to the toast element. |
| `pauseOnHover` | boolean | `true` | Whether to pause the auto-dismiss timer on hover. Focus inside the toast pauses it whatever this is set to. |
| `closeAriaLabel` | string | `"Close notification"` | Accessible label for the close button. |
| `aria-label` | string | — | Accessible name of the toast's status region. |
| `aria-labelledby` | string | — | Ids of the elements that name the toast's status region. |
| `aria-describedby` | string | — | Ids of the elements that describe the toast's status region. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | When true, removes all default styling. |

### Sub-component Props

Generated from the types by `scripts/build-subcomponent-schemas.mjs`.

#### ToastProvider

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Content rendered inside this element. |
| `position` | `ToastPosition \| undefined` | Toast position on screen. Default: `"bottom-right"`. |
| `maxToasts` | `number \| undefined` | How many toasts may be visible at once. Older ones leave as new ones arrive. |
| `containerClassName` | `string \| undefined` | Additional classes for the toast container. |
| `defaultDuration` | `number \| undefined` | How long a toast stays up, in milliseconds, when it does not set its own. |
| `animationDuration` | `number \| undefined` | Enter and exit transition duration in milliseconds. |
| `gap` | `number \| undefined` | Space between stacked toasts, in pixels. |
| `zIndex` | `number \| undefined` | Stacking order for the toast container. |
| `closeOnEscape` | `boolean \| undefined` | Dismisses the newest toast when Escape is pressed, unless something above it — an open dialog, drawer or menu — has already handled the key. On by default. |
| `containerAriaLabel` | `string \| undefined` | Accessible name for the toast region. |
| `classes` | `ToastClasses \| undefined` | Class overrides for this component's slots. |
| `unstyled` | `boolean \| undefined` | Drops the decorative default classes and keeps the structural ones, along with focus, keyboard and ARIA wiring. |

---

### Data Attributes (for CSS selectors and testing)

- `data-toast-id` — on each toast, the id the API returns from `toast.success(...)`
- `data-variant="default" | "success" | "error" | "warning" | "info"` — the variant

---

### Class overrides

#### Slot → element

| Slot | Element |
|------|---------|
| `root` | The toast surface — the coloured card the whole notice sits on. |
| `body` | The padded row inside `root` holding the icon, the message and the close button. |
| `range` | The fill inside `track`, which shrinks as the auto-dismiss timer runs. |
| `icon` | The icon wrapper. |
| `title` | The message line, which is the toast's accessible name. |
| `description` | The description under it. |
| `track` | The auto-dismiss progress groove. |
| `closeTrigger` | The dismiss button. |

#### CSS custom properties

Each variant reads three, written as Tailwind arbitrary values with the
library's colour as the fallback — `bg-[var(--toast-default-bg,#374151)]`. Set
them on any ancestor to retheme toasts without touching `classes`.

| Variable | Controls | Default |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--toast-default-bg` / `--toast-default-border` / `--toast-default-text` | the neutral toast | `#374151` / `#374151` / `white` |
| `--toast-success-bg` / `--toast-success-border` / `--toast-success-text` | the success variant | the library's success palette |
| `--toast-error-bg` / `--toast-error-border` / `--toast-error-text` | the error variant | the library's error palette |
| `--toast-warning-bg` / `--toast-warning-border` / `--toast-warning-text` | the warning variant | the library's warning palette |
| `--toast-info-bg` / `--toast-info-border` / `--toast-info-text` | the info variant | the library's info palette |

---

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

Toast supports CSS custom variables for theming:
- `--toast-success-bg`, `--toast-success-border`, `--toast-success-text`
- Same pattern for warning, error, info, default

Or use `classes` prop with 7 slots: container, content, message, description, progress, closeButton, icon.

---

---

## Tooltip

> Accessible tooltip with configurable positioning, delays, rich content, arrows, shadows, truncation, and full dark mode support.

**Category:** Overlay
**Keywords:** tooltip, popover, hover, hint, help text, info bubble, title

### Import

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from "@chumlab/ui/tooltip";
```

---

### Basic Usage (copy-paste ready)

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from "@chumlab/ui/tooltip";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip content="Save your changes">
      <button>Hover me</button>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

---

### Prop Constraints

| Prop | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| `side` | `"top"` (default), `"right"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"` |
| `align` | `"center"` (default), `"start"`, `"end"` |
| `content` | ReactNode — string or JSX for rich tooltips |
| `truncate` | When true, trigger text truncates and tooltip shows full text on hover |
| `open` + `onOpenChange` | Controlled mode |
| `shadow` | Preset (`"none"` to `"2xl"`) or custom CSS shadow string |
| `asChild` | Merges trigger props onto the child element instead of wrapping |

#### A tooltip on an interactive element: `asChild`

When the trigger is a button, a link or any focusable component, including this library's own
`Button`, make that element the only child and set `asChild`. The tooltip's handlers and its
`aria-describedby` go onto it, so it keeps its single tab stop and a screen reader reads the
tooltip when it takes focus.

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Delete the file" asChild>
  <Button aria-label="Delete">…</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

Without `asChild`, a focusable direct child is detected and given the description, but a
focusable element nested inside another one is not: the wrapper takes the description, and the
control that receives focus announces nothing.

---

### All Props

<!-- generated from Tooltip.schema.json — edit the schema, not this table -->

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` **(required)** | object | — | React.ReactNode — The trigger element that the tooltip is attached to. |
| `content` | object | — | React.ReactNode — Content displayed inside the tooltip. |
| `side` | `"top"` \| `"right"` \| `"bottom"` \| `"left"` | `"top"` | Preferred side of the trigger to display the tooltip. |
| `align` | `"start"` \| `"center"` \| `"end"` | `"center"` | Alignment of the tooltip along the side. |
| `sideOffset` | number | `6` | Distance in pixels from the trigger along the side axis. |
| `alignOffset` | number | `0` | Offset in pixels along the alignment axis. |
| `maxWidth` | string \| number | `300` | Maximum width of the tooltip content. |
| `wordWrap` | `"normal"` \| `"break-word"` \| `"nowrap"` | `"break-word"` | Word wrap behavior for tooltip content. |
| `delayDuration` | number | `200` | Delay in milliseconds before showing the tooltip. |
| `hideDelayDuration` | number | `100` | Delay in milliseconds before hiding the tooltip. |
| `hoverableContent` | boolean | `true` | Keeps the tooltip open while the pointer moves onto it (WCAG 1.4.13). `false` closes it as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger. |
| `open` | boolean | — | Controlled open state. |
| `defaultOpen` | boolean | `false` | Default uncontrolled open state. |
| `onOpenChange` | object | — | (open: boolean) => void — Callback when the open state changes. |
| `showArrow` | boolean | `true` | Whether to show the tooltip arrow. |
| `arrowSize` | number | — | Size of the tooltip arrow in pixels. |
| `arrowColor` | string | — | Color of the tooltip arrow. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Whether the tooltip is disabled. |
| `truncate` | boolean | `false` | Whether to truncate the trigger content with ellipsis. |
| `truncateWidth` | number \| string | — | Width at which to truncate the trigger content. |
| `shadow` | string | `"lg"` | Shadow preset or custom CSS shadow value. Presets: 'none', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', '2xl'. |
| `zIndex` | number | `9999` | Z-index for the tooltip. |
| `portal` | boolean | `true` | Whether to render the tooltip in a portal. |
| `portalContainer` | object | — | HTMLElement \| null — Custom container element for the tooltip portal. Read only when `portal` is true; with `portal={false}` it chooses nothing. |
| `asChild` | boolean | `false` | When true, the trigger renders as the child element instead of wrapping it. |
| `triggerDisplay` | string | `"inline-flex"` | CSS display property for the trigger wrapper. |
| `className` | string | — | CSS class for the trigger wrapper element. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the trigger wrapper element, with `className`. |
| `id` | string | — | Id of the element that takes focus: the child it wraps, or the wrapper around plain text. Wins over the child's own. |
| `aria-label` | string | — | Accessible name of the element that takes focus: the child it wraps, or the wrapper around plain text. Wins over the child's own. |
| `aria-labelledby` | string | — | Ids of the elements that name the element that takes focus: the child it wraps, or the wrapper around plain text. Wins over the child's own. |
| `aria-describedby` | string | — | Ids of the elements that describe the element that takes focus: the child it wraps, or the wrapper around plain text; joined after the child's own and before the tooltip's id while it is open. |
| `classes` | object | — | CSS class overrides for sub-elements. |
| `unstyled` | boolean | `false` | When true, removes all default styling. |
| `contentStyle` | object | — | Inline styles applied to the tooltip content element. |
| `arrowStyle` | object | — | Inline styles applied to the tooltip arrow element. |
| `baseArrowStyle` | object | — | Inline styles applied to the base arrow element. |

### Styling Guide

> **A plain utility replaces the library's for that property, in every state.**
> `classes={{ slot: "text-red-500" }}` drops the library's `hover:text-…` and
> `data-[state=…]:text-…` on that slot as well — otherwise they would sit beside
> your class and win in their own state, leaving your override in the DOM and
> inert. Pass your own variant to keep one: `"text-red-500 hover:text-red-400"`.
> A variant YOU pass is never dropped.

#### Slots

```
trigger (span wrapper, or merged via asChild)
└── portal
    └── content (role="tooltip", positioned)
        ├── children (tooltip text/JSX)
        └── arrow (CSS triangle)
```

| Slot | What it styles |
|------|---------------|
| `trigger` | Wrapper around the child element |
| `content` | Tooltip popup (bg, border, padding, text) |
| `arrow` | Arrow triangle fill |
| `arrow` | Arrow border/outline |

#### Dark mode

Defaults include `dark:` variants. Content uses `bg-white dark:bg-gray-800`, `text-gray-900 dark:text-white`, `border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700`.

---

### Keyboard Interactions

| Key | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the trigger, which shows the tooltip — hover is not the only way in. |
| `Escape` | Hides it while the trigger keeps focus. Always: there is no prop to turn it off, because WCAG 1.4.13 requires hover or focus content to be dismissible. |

---
